general_skills.title: Apply Theorems to Relate Segments
general_skills.principle: Use established geometric theorems (e.g., Angle Bisector Theorem, Stewart’s Theorem) to derive proportional relationships or length constraints in a figure.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves cevians, ratios, or lengths in a triangle with known side lengths.

general_skills.title: Solve Algebraic Equations for Target Quantities
general_skills.principle: Set up and solve equations derived from geometric relationships to compute the desired value, ensuring consistency with all given constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem requires combining proportional relationships with algebraic manipulation to isolate the target expression.

general_skills.title: Constraint Decomposition
general_skills.principle: Break complex conditions into simpler, independent constraints by introducing auxiliary variables or transformations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves multiple interdependent variables and nonlinear relationships.

general_skills.title: Iterative Counting with Bounds
general_skills.principle: Systematically iterate over possible parameter ranges, applying upper/lower bounds to count valid cases efficiently.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When enumerating solutions to discrete problems with clear numerical constraints.

general_skills.title: Fraction Simplification via GCD
general_skills.principle: Reduce fractions by computing the greatest common divisor of numerator and denominator.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When expressing probabilities or ratios in lowest terms.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Geometry Modeling
general_skills.principle: Represent geometric configurations with coordinates to derive algebraic relationships between points and segments.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When spatial relationships involve recursive constructions or proportional divisions.

general_skills.title: Similarity Ratio Application
general_skills.principle: Use similarity properties to establish proportional relationships between corresponding sides and areas of similar figures.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When problems involve iterative scaling or recursive geometric subdivisions.

general_skills.title: Geometric Series Summation
general_skills.principle: Recognize patterns forming geometric sequences and apply the infinite series formula to compute cumulative quantities.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing processes with diminishing contributions that converge to a finite limit.

general_skills.title: Modular Constraint Categorization
general_skills.principle: Transform complex constraints into residue classes using modular arithmetic to simplify analysis and identify patterns.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When constraints involve divisibility or periodicity conditions that can be expressed via modular arithmetic.

general_skills.title: Cyclic Pattern Recognition
general_skills.principle: Identify repeating residue patterns in cyclic sequences to group elements into classes that satisfy the problem's constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with circular arrangements or conditions that impose periodic relationships between elements.

general_skills.title: Symmetry Adjustment via Division
general_skills.principle: Account for rotational symmetry by dividing the total count by the number of rotational symmetries when all arrangements are asymmetric.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When counting distinct arrangements under rotational equivalence and no non-trivial symmetries exist.

general_skills.title: Factorial Simplification via Product Decomposition
general_skills.principle: Express factorial ratios (like n!/k!) as products of consecutive integers to simplify computations, especially when multiplied by terms involving factorials.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with expressions involving factorials in the denominator and a factorial multiplier, such as n! * (k² - 2)/k!.

general_skills.title: Modular Reduction of Large Products
general_skills.principle: Break down large products into smaller segments, applying modulo operations incrementally to manage computational complexity and avoid overflow.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When calculating the last few digits of a product or sum involving large factorials or combinatorial terms.

general_skills.title: Term Decomposition for Modular Arithmetic
general_skills.principle: Decompose complex terms (e.g., k² - 2) into simpler components and compute each part modulo the target value to streamline calculations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When evaluating sums or products modulo a number, especially with polynomial-like terms in the numerator.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Geometry Modeling
general_skills.principle: Assign coordinates to geometric figures to translate geometric constraints into algebraic equations, enabling precise calculation of distances, slopes, and intersections.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves spatial relationships that can be represented with coordinates, such as triangles, lines, or shapes with known side lengths.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis for Ambiguous Configurations
general_skills.principle: Systematically explore all possible configurations (e.g., different pairs of parallel sides) that satisfy the problem's conditions to identify valid solutions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiple interpretations or configurations of a geometric condition exist, such as parallelism or tangency, leading to distinct solution paths.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Equation Solving
general_skills.principle: Derive and solve systems of equations based on geometric constraints (e.g., distance formulas, slopes) to determine coordinates or other quantitative relationships.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When geometric relationships can be expressed algebraically, such as finding intersections, lengths, or ratios through equations.

general_skills.title: Geometric Constraints to Algebraic Equations
general_skills.principle: Translate geometric conditions (e.g., tangent angles) into algebraic equations using derivatives or parametric relationships.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem specifies geometric properties that can be expressed via slopes, angles, or curve parameters.

general_skills.title: Integral Simplification via Substitution
general_skills.principle: Simplify complex integrals by identifying substitutions that linearize or decouple variables, reducing computational complexity.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When evaluating integrals involving nonlinear terms, especially in arc length or area calculations.

general_skills.title: Pattern Matching for Answer Forms
general_skills.principle: Reorganize expressions to match target forms by factoring, expanding, or isolating terms, ensuring alignment with problem-specific formatting requirements.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When final answers must conform to structured formats (e.g., $\frac{a}{b}(c\sqrt{d} - e)$) for summation or verification.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Extraction
general_skills.principle: Identify and extract coordinates from visual or code-based representations to use in calculations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem provides coordinates in diagrams, code, or explicit lists.

general_skills.title: Distance Formula Application
general_skills.principle: Use the distance formula between two points to compute lengths in coordinate geometry problems.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When calculating side lengths or distances between vertices in coordinate-based figures.

general_skills.title: Polygon Area Calculation
general_skills.principle: Apply the shoelace formula or equivalent coordinate-based methods to determine the area of polygons with known vertices.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When calculating the area of a polygon with integer coordinates or other coordinate data.

general_skills.title: Minimize Denominator via Structural Optimization
general_skills.principle: Identify scenarios where the operation (e.g., multiplication) results in a number with minimal digit sum, such as powers of 10, to reduce the denominator of the ratio.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When optimizing a ratio involving digit sums and the operation can produce numbers with minimal digit sums (e.g., powers of 10).

general_skills.title: Maximize Numerator with Digit Sum Constraints
general_skills.principle: Select numbers that maximize the numerator's digit sum while satisfying constraints imposed by the denominator's minimization, such as trailing zeros to avoid increasing the digit sum.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When balancing numerator and denominator in a ratio, prioritize numbers with high digit sums that align with the denominator's structural requirements.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis for Edge Conditions
general_skills.principle: Split the problem into cases based on number structures (e.g., powers of 10) that can lead to extreme values of the ratio, then eliminate invalid cases through verification.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When exploring extremal values of a ratio, use case analysis to isolate configurations that could yield minimal/maximal outcomes.

general_skills.title: Volume Conservation for Reshaped Objects
general_skills.principle: When objects can be reshaped but not compressed, the total volume of the objects must not exceed the container's volume. Compute the container's volume and divide by the volume of a single object to determine the maximum number that can fit.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem involves reshaping objects without compression, and the goal is to determine how many such objects can fit into a container.

general_skills.title: Volume Ratio for Packing Constraints
general_skills.principle: Use the ratio of the container's volume to the volume of a single object to determine the maximum number of objects that can fit, considering volume as the limiting factor.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem requires comparing the total volume of objects to a container's volume, especially when objects can be reformed into any shape.

general_skills.title: Model with Geometric Distributions
general_skills.principle: Recognize that the number of trials until the first success in independent trials follows a geometric distribution, characterized by the probability of success per trial.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing waiting times for the first success in independent, identically distributed trials.

general_skills.title: Conditional Expectation with Ratio Constraints
general_skills.principle: Express the target expectation as a conditional probability, leveraging given ratio constraints between variables to derive algebraic relationships.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving for expectations under explicit relationships between random variables (e.g., one variable is a scalar multiple of another).

general_skills.title: Fraction Simplification via Coprimality Checks
general_skills.principle: Reduce fractions by factoring numerator and denominator into primes and eliminating common factors, ensuring the final fraction is in lowest terms.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When final answers require reduced fractional forms, particularly in problems involving modular arithmetic or combinatorial coefficients.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis for Constraints
general_skills.principle: Partition the problem into distinct, mutually exclusive cases that capture all constraint scenarios, ensuring each case satisfies the problem's conditions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When constraints involve conditional relationships between elements (e.g., exclusions, dependencies).

general_skills.title: Permutation with Restricted Choices
general_skills.principle: Calculate permutations by first selecting elements that meet constraints, then assigning roles or positions while respecting uniqueness and restrictions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When arranging distinct items with limitations on selection or placement (e.g., forbidden pairs, role-specific rules).

general_skills.title: Sum Valid Case Contributions
general_skills.principle: Aggregate results from all valid cases by summing their individual counts, ensuring no overlap or omission.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving combinatorial problems requiring exhaustive enumeration of valid configurations.

general_skills.title: Union Bound for Lower Bounds
general_skills.principle: The probability of the intersection of two events is bounded below by the sum of their probabilities minus 1. This arises from the constraint that the probability of their union cannot exceed 1.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When given individual probabilities of two events and needing a lower bound on their joint probability.

general_skills.title: Minimization for Upper Bounds
general_skills.principle: The probability of the intersection of two events cannot exceed the smaller of their individual probabilities, as the intersection cannot be larger than either event alone.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining an upper bound for the joint probability of two events based on their individual probabilities.

general_skills.title: Leverage Reflection Properties
general_skills.principle: When a figure is folded over a line, that line acts as the perpendicular bisector of the segment connecting a point and its image. Use this to establish congruent distances and symmetry relationships.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with folding, reflection, or mirroring transformations in geometry.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Geometry Modeling
general_skills.principle: Assign coordinates to geometric figures to convert spatial relationships into algebraic equations, enabling systematic computation of lengths, slopes, and intersections.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When visualizing complex geometric configurations or needing precise measurements.

general_skills.title: Identify Algebraic Invariants
general_skills.principle: Simplify expressions to reveal constants or invariants that remain unchanged despite variable parameters, often through substitution or symmetry analysis.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving problems with variable components that unexpectedly yield fixed results.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Manipulation via Equation Transformation
general_skills.principle: Rewrite equations to isolate variables by applying inverse operations, preserving equality constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving for an unknown in an equation involving multiple variables.

general_skills.title: Constraint-Driven Equation Formation
general_skills.principle: Use known properties (e.g., imaginary part of a complex number) to create equations that directly relate to the target variable.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When specific constraints or properties of the problem are provided and can be translated into mathematical equations.

general_skills.title: Sum of Odd Numbers Identity
general_skills.principle: Recognize that the sum of the first n odd numbers equals n squared (1 + 3 + 5 + ... + (2n-1) = n²).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When encountering a sequence of odd numbers with incremental step sizes.

general_skills.title: Range Interpretation with Examples
general_skills.principle: Use given examples and problem constraints to infer plausible values within a range, prioritizing values that align with known patterns or simplifications.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem specifies a range for a variable and provides illustrative examples.

general_skills.title: Total to Distribution Conversion
general_skills.principle: Determine the quantity per group by dividing the total quantity by the number of groups, ensuring divisibility and consistency with problem constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When distributing a total quantity evenly across multiple groups with equal shares.

general_skills.title: Ratio-Based Variable Assignment
general_skills.principle: Assign variables based on given ratios to convert geometric constraints into algebraic equations, enabling quantitative analysis.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When ratios of lengths or segments are provided in a geometric configuration.

general_skills.title: Trigonometric Equation Simplification
general_skills.principle: Use trigonometric identities to simplify equations involving angles and sides, transforming complex expressions into solvable forms.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving for angles or sides in triangles with known or derived angle relationships.

general_skills.title: Standard Value Recognition
general_skills.principle: Identify and leverage known trigonometric values (e.g., tan(75°) = 2 + √3) to directly determine angle measures from simplified equations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When an equation reduces to a standard trigonometric identity or known value.

general_skills.title: Pattern Recognition in Sequences
general_skills.principle: Identify patterns or properties that allow a complex sequence or sum to be simplified into a known form (e.g., arithmetic/geometric series).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When confronted with a problem involving sums or sequences that appear intractable at first glance.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Simplification for Divisibility
general_skills.principle: Transform ratios or expressions into simplified fractional forms to uncover divisibility conditions or integer constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing ratios or expressions that require determining when they evaluate to integers.

general_skills.title: Divisibility Condition Analysis
general_skills.principle: Determine when a variable divides a constant by reducing the problem to finding all divisors of the constant, leveraging modular arithmetic properties.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem requires identifying values of a variable that make a ratio or expression an integer.

general_skills.title: Leverage Given Data Through Division
general_skills.principle: When a related product is provided, isolate the target component by dividing the known product by the product of non-target elements in the same range.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the target product overlaps with a known product that includes both target and non-target elements.

general_skills.title: Decompose Products into Manageable Segments
general_skills.principle: Break complex products into smaller, independent segments that can be computed or referenced individually, then combine results.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When direct computation of the target product is infeasible due to size or complexity.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Simplification
general_skills.principle: Simplify complex equations by combining like terms and reducing them to a form that reveals relationships between variables.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When an equation involves multiple variables and constraints, such as digit relationships in number theory problems.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis Based on Constraints
general_skills.principle: Split the problem into cases based on the most constrained variable (e.g., leading digit in a number) to narrow down possibilities systematically.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When variables have bounded ranges or discrete values, such as digits in a number or combinatorial selections.

general_skills.title: Iterative Verification of Minimality
general_skills.principle: After identifying a potential solution, verify it by checking smaller cases or values to ensure no valid solution was overlooked.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the goal is to find the minimal or maximal solution, such as in optimization problems or number theory.

general_skills.title: Apply Euclidean Algorithm for GCD Reduction
general_skills.principle: Reduce GCD problems by repeatedly applying the Euclidean algorithm, replacing the larger number with its modulus relative to the smaller number until reaching a base case.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When computing GCDs involving polynomials or integers, especially when one operand is a multiple of another.

general_skills.title: Simplify Expressions via Modular Arithmetic
general_skills.principle: Use modular arithmetic to eliminate higher-degree terms in polynomials by recognizing that the remainder upon division by a variable is the constant term.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When simplifying algebraic expressions or evaluating remainders in polynomial divisions.

general_skills.title: Factor Numbers to Identify Common Divisors
general_skills.principle: Factor integers into prime components to determine shared divisors, leveraging divisibility relationships between numbers and their multiples.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing GCDs involving multiples or divisors, particularly when one number is a known multiple of another.

general_skills.title: Extremal Value Allocation
general_skills.principle: To optimize a sum under constraints, assign variables to their extremal values (e.g., lower or upper bounds) to maximize/minimize the target function's contribution.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When variables have bounded domains and the objective function is sensitive to extreme values.

general_skills.title: Constraint-Based Variable Grouping
general_skills.principle: Partition variables into groups with fixed values and unknowns to simplify constraint satisfaction through algebraic equations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with multiple variables and constraints that can be decoupled via symmetry or boundary conditions.

general_skills.title: Optimality via Perturbation
general_skills.principle: Verify a solution's optimality by testing small deviations from the candidate solution to ensure no lower/higher value exists.
general_skills.when_to_apply: After deriving a candidate solution, to confirm it is minimal/maximal under the given constraints.

general_skills.title: Cyclic Configuration Insight
general_skills.principle: When points lie on a common circle, the circumcenter of any three non-collinear points is the center of the circle. This allows identifying the center as the only equidistant point.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with points on a circle or cyclic configurations, recognize that the circumcenter of any subset of three non-collinear points is the circle's center.

general_skills.title: Uniqueness of Circumcenter
general_skills.principle: For any triangle, the circumcenter is unique. Thus, if three points lie on a circle, their circumcenter is the circle's center, eliminating other equidistant points.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing equidistant points to three non-collinear points, use the uniqueness of the circumcenter to constrain solutions to the circle's center.

general_skills.title: Telescoping Recurrence Relations
general_skills.principle: When a functional equation defines a recurrence, express the target value as a telescoping sum by iterating the equation, allowing terms to cancel or combine systematically.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving for a term in a sequence defined by a recurrence relation involving overlapping terms.

general_skills.title: Summation Formula Application
general_skills.principle: Identify patterns in derived sums (e.g., alternating series) and apply known summation formulas to simplify complex expressions into closed-form results.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When confronted with sums involving polynomial terms and alternating signs, recognize standard summation identities to reduce computational complexity.

general_skills.title: Modular Arithmetic Finalization
general_skills.principle: Compute the target value explicitly and apply modular arithmetic to extract the required remainder, ensuring precision with large numbers.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem requires a remainder or residue after computing a large value, use modular arithmetic to isolate the desired result.

general_skills.title: Verify Parity Conditions
general_skills.principle: Check that the total area is even and that the number of squares with even/odd coordinate sums (i+j) is balanced, as dominoes cover one square of each parity.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When tiling with dominoes requires matching counts of two complementary subsets (e.g., checkerboard colors).

general_skills.title: Compute Parity-Based Counts
general_skills.principle: For an odd-sized grid, calculate the number of squares with a specific parity (e.g., i+j even) using the formula (m² + 1)/2, leveraging the imbalance in odd dimensions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining the count of elements in a grid with a parity constraint, especially for odd-sized regions.

general_skills.title: Unify Equal Logarithmic Expressions
general_skills.principle: When multiple logarithmic expressions are equal, set them equal to a common variable and convert each to exponential form to express variables in terms of that variable.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with systems of logarithmic equations with shared values.

general_skills.title: Substitute Derived Expressions into Constraints
general_skills.principle: Substitute variables expressed in terms of a common parameter into the main equation to form a constraint equation, enabling algebraic manipulation and solution for the parameter.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When variables are expressed parametrically and need to satisfy a primary equation or inequality.

general_skills.title: Analyze Functional Behavior for Validity
general_skills.principle: Analyze the behavior of functions (e.g., monotonicity, extrema) to determine valid solutions, especially when optimizing expressions or resolving ambiguities in parameter values.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving for parameters in exponential or logarithmic contexts where multiple solutions may exist.

general_skills.title: Categorize Lines by Slope
general_skills.principle: Group lines by their slope to systematically count distinct lines, ensuring all geometric configurations are addressed without duplication.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When enumerating lines through points in a grid or discrete set, especially when multiple points lie on the same line.

general_skills.title: Enumerate All Possible Slopes
general_skills.principle: Systematically consider all unique slopes between pairs of points to avoid missing cases and ensure completeness in counting.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing configurations requiring exhaustive case analysis, such as counting lines or paths in a grid.

general_skills.title: Adjust for Overlapping Cases
general_skills.principle: Recognize and account for lines that pass through multiple points to prevent overcounting, using geometric properties to identify such overlaps.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When calculating quantities that involve shared elements (e.g., lines, sets, or paths) across multiple pairs.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Geometry Modeling
general_skills.principle: Represent geometric configurations with coordinates to translate problems into algebraic equations, enabling precise calculations of intersections and distances.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves complex intersections, ratios, or unknown lengths that can be expressed via coordinate relationships.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Intersection Solving
general_skills.principle: Solve systems of equations derived from lines and circles to determine critical points like intersections or circumcircle points.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When geometric relationships require finding exact coordinates or parameters of intersecting figures.

general_skills.title: Proportional Reasoning in Similar Figures
general_skills.principle: Apply ratios from similar triangles or intersecting diagonals in trapezoids to deduce segment lengths and proportional divisions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with intersecting diagonals, parallel lines, or similar figures that create proportional relationships.

general_skills.title: Model Cyclic Systems as State Transitions
general_skills.principle: Represent problems with cyclic or symmetric structures as state machines where each state's transitions follow defined rules. This allows leveraging recurrence relations or matrix exponentiation to track probabilities or counts over steps.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem involves periodic behavior, wrap-around transitions, or symmetric state interactions.

general_skills.title: Solve Linear Recurrences for Probabilistic Patterns
general_skills.principle: Identify and solve linear recurrence relations to derive closed-form expressions for probabilities or counts. This often involves finding eigenvalues, characteristic equations, or exploiting symmetry to simplify computations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When repeated transitions or steps generate patterns that can be expressed recursively, especially in probabilistic or combinatorial contexts.

general_skills.title: Compute Large Exponents via Modular Decomposition
general_skills.principle: Break down large exponents using modular arithmetic properties (e.g., Euler's theorem, Chinese Remainder Theorem) to simplify computations. Focus on reducing the modulus to manageable components before recombining results.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When evaluating expressions with massive exponents modulo a number, particularly in number theory or combinatorics problems.

general_skills.title: Decompose Numbers by Digit Places
general_skills.principle: Break down multi-digit numbers into their constituent place values (hundreds, tens, ones) to analyze digit frequency systematically.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When counting occurrences of digits in ranges of numbers with consistent place-value patterns.

general_skills.title: Aggregate Digit Frequencies
general_skills.principle: Calculate the total occurrences of each digit across all positions (units, tens, hundreds) by analyzing ranges and overlapping patterns.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining resource requirements based on digit usage in sequential or structured number sets.

general_skills.title: Maximize Resource Allocation
general_skills.principle: Determine the required quantity of resources (e.g., digit packages) by identifying the maximum demand for any single component.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When resources are bundled to cover multiple components, and the limiting factor is the highest individual requirement.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Geometry Modeling
general_skills.principle: Assign coordinates to geometric elements to translate the problem into algebraic terms, enabling calculation of lengths, areas, and ratios.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem involves geometric figures with measurable lengths and ratios.

general_skills.title: Linear Interpolation for Point Location
general_skills.principle: Use linear interpolation along a line segment to determine coordinates of points based on given ratios of distances.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When points are defined proportionally along a line segment.

general_skills.title: Area Calculation via Coordinates
general_skills.principle: Compute areas of polygons using coordinate-based formulas (e.g., determinant method) and simplify ratios of areas.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When comparing areas in coordinate geometry problems.

general_skills.title: Sum Formula Application
general_skills.principle: Express sums of consecutive integers using general formulas (e.g., sum of squares) to translate word problems into algebraic equations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves sums of sequences or requires relating sums of different lengths.

general_skills.title: Incremental Case Testing
general_skills.principle: Systematically test small values of parameters (e.g., n) to identify minimal solutions or patterns that satisfy constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When seeking minimal integers or verifying feasibility of conditions with variable parameters.

general_skills.title: Equation Substitution and Simplification
general_skills.principle: Substitute derived expressions into each other to form equations that relate variables, then simplify to find relationships or specific values.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiple expressions represent the same quantity under different conditions or constraints.

general_skills.title: Decompose Totient Expressions with Multiplicative Properties
general_skills.principle: Use the multiplicative formula φ(ab) = φ(a)φ(b) * gcd(a,b)/φ(gcd(a,b)) to break down complex totient expressions into components based on prime factors and gcd relationships.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving equations involving φ(n) for composite arguments, especially with products of constants and variables.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis via Prime Factor Divisibility
general_skills.principle: Classify solutions by analyzing divisibility of the variable by primes present in the problem's constants to handle gcd interactions systematically.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When equations involve gcd terms with multiple primes, to isolate valid scenarios based on variable factorization.

general_skills.title: Substitute Known Totient Values to Simplify Equations
general_skills.principle: Replace φ of constants with precomputed values to reduce the equation to a form dependent on the variable's factors, enabling targeted analysis.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When equations contain φ of fixed constants, to simplify and focus on variable-dependent terms.

general_skills.title: Apply Geometric Constraints Algebraically
general_skills.principle: Translate geometric conditions (e.g., triangle inequality) into algebraic inequalities that can be systematically analyzed and counted.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem requires verifying relationships between variables (e.g., triangle inequality, distance constraints, or ordering conditions).

general_skills.title: Use Summation Formulas for Combinatorial Counts
general_skills.principle: Leverage known summation formulas (e.g., sum of squares, sum of integers) to compute totals for structured combinatorial problems efficiently.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When counting cases with symmetric or recursive structures, such as permutations, combinations, or range-based aggregations.

general_skills.title: Simplify Fractions to Lowest Terms
general_skills.principle: Reduce fractions by identifying and dividing numerator and denominator by their greatest common divisor (GCD), ensuring coprimality of the final result.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When expressing probabilities or ratios in reduced form, particularly when the problem guarantees coprimality of the final fraction.

general_skills.title: Variable Substitution for Reduction
general_skills.principle: Express variables in terms of others to reduce the system to a single equation involving the target parameter, enabling direct solution.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiple variables and equations exist, and the goal is to solve for a specific parameter.

general_skills.title: Boundary Case Analysis
general_skills.principle: Assume variables take extreme values (e.g., zero) to simplify constraints and identify minimal/maximal solutions under non-negativity conditions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When optimizing a parameter under non-negativity or inequality constraints.

general_skills.title: Solution Verification via Substitution
general_skills.principle: Plug candidate solutions back into original equations to confirm they satisfy all constraints and yield valid results.
general_skills.when_to_apply: After deriving a potential solution, to ensure correctness and compliance with problem conditions.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis Based on Function Conditions
general_skills.principle: When a function has conditional behavior (e.g., parity-based rules), split the problem into cases corresponding to each condition and analyze their distinct dynamics.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a function or process exhibits different behaviors based on input properties (e.g., even/odd, divisibility).

general_skills.title: Trace Function Behavior to Identify Termination Paths
general_skills.principle: For iterative functions, trace the transformation of small inputs to detect patterns or invariants that determine whether the process reaches a target state.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing recursive or repeated applications of a function to determine convergence or termination.

general_skills.title: Identify Necessary Conditions for Termination
general_skills.principle: Determine properties (e.g., structural constraints like powers of 2) that are required for a process to reach a target, and count inputs satisfying these properties.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem requires counting inputs that eventually satisfy a condition through a defined transformation.

general_skills.title: Difference-Based Divisor Identification
general_skills.principle: When two numbers leave remainders r1 and r2 when divided by a common divisor d, the difference between the numbers is divisible by d. This allows identifying d as a divisor of the difference.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When given two numbers with known remainders when divided by the same divisor.

general_skills.title: Remainder Constraint Enforcement
general_skills.principle: The divisor must be larger than any remainder in the problem. This ensures the remainder condition (r < d) is satisfied.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving problems involving division with remainders.

general_skills.title: Candidate Verification via Modular Testing
general_skills.principle: Generate candidate divisors from the difference's divisors that meet size constraints and verify them against the original remainder conditions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When narrowing down possible divisors using difference-based constraints.

general_skills.title: Factor Exponents for Simplification
general_skills.principle: Factor out common exponential terms to reduce complex expressions into simpler components, revealing dominant terms that dictate the expression's behavior.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with expressions involving exponents that differ by a fixed amount, such as $ a^{n+k} + b^{n+k} $ divided by $ a^n + b^n $.

general_skills.title: Bound Expressions via Dominant Terms
general_skills.principle: Estimate the value of an expression by isolating dominant terms and analyzing the contribution of smaller terms to establish upper and lower bounds.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When an expression contains terms that grow or shrink exponentially, and the goal is to determine its integer part or approximate value.

general_skills.title: Apply Angle Bisector Theorem for Segment Ratios
general_skills.principle: When an angle bisector divides a segment, use the Angle Bisector Theorem to establish proportional relationships between the divided segments.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When an angle bisector intersects a line segment, and segment ratios are needed to relate lengths.

general_skills.title: Translate Geometric Constraints into Algebraic Equations
general_skills.principle: Introduce variables for unknown lengths and derive equations based on given ratios, constraints, and geometric properties.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When direct geometric relationships are insufficient, and algebraic modeling is required to connect variables.

general_skills.title: Solve Equations via Substitution and Simplification
general_skills.principle: Leverage known values and derived relationships to substitute into equations, simplifying step-by-step to isolate the target quantity.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiple equations exist and substitution simplifies the system to solve for an unknown.

general_skills.title: Similarity and Area Scaling
general_skills.principle: When a geometric figure undergoes a similarity transformation, its area scales by the square of the ratio of corresponding linear dimensions. Use this relationship to derive proportional relationships between original and transformed figures.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with scaled copies of geometric shapes, especially polygons, and needing to compute area changes.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Simplification with Radicals
general_skills.principle: Simplify expressions involving radicals by expanding squared terms, factoring, and combining like terms, ensuring the final form matches the required structure (e.g., √k - m).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When manipulating algebraic expressions with radicals to achieve a specific target form, such as solving for variables in nested radical expressions.

general_skills.title: Constraint-Based Value Restriction
general_skills.principle: When variables and their reciprocals must be integers, restrict variables to values that satisfy both conditions (e.g., ±1) by solving for integer constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem requires variables and their reciprocals to be integers or other algebraic constraints.

general_skills.title: Combinatorial Case Enumeration
general_skills.principle: Systematically list all combinations of variables within their constrained values to explore all possible cases.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When variables are limited to a small, finite set of possibilities and the problem requires evaluating all combinations.

general_skills.title: Distinct Outcome Verification
general_skills.principle: Compute all possible results from valid combinations and identify distinct values through exhaustive checking.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem requires counting unique results, such as sums, products, or other derived quantities.

general_skills.title: Decompose Constraints into Independent Subproblems
general_skills.principle: When multiple constraints exist, identify and separate independent subproblems that can be solved individually and then combined.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When constraints involve distinct groups or variables with no overlapping dependencies.

general_skills.title: Subtract Invalid Cases from Total Possibilities
general_skills.principle: Calculate the total number of unrestricted combinations, then subtract configurations that violate specific constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When direct counting of valid cases is complex, but invalid cases can be enumerated systematically.

general_skills.title: Multiply Valid Options for Independent Choices
general_skills.principle: If choices are independent across different groups, multiply the number of valid options for each group to obtain the total combinations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When distinct groups make decisions without influencing each other's options.

general_skills.title: Leverage Parallel Lines for Angle Relationships
general_skills.principle: When parallel lines are intersected by transversals, corresponding angles are equal. Use this to establish congruent angles or supplementary relationships in geometric configurations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When parallel lines and transversals create angles that can be equated or related through their positions.

general_skills.title: Relate Inscribed Angles to Subtended Arcs
general_skills.principle: An inscribed angle's measure is half the measure of its subtended arc. Use this to connect angle measures to arc measures in circles.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When calculating angles formed by points on a circle, identify the arc they subtend and apply the inscribed angle theorem.

general_skills.title: Use Ratios to Determine Proportional Angles
general_skills.principle: If angles are in a known ratio, assign variables based on the ratio and solve for their measures using algebraic relationships.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When angles are given in a proportional relationship, express them algebraically and solve using the ratio constraints.

general_skills.title: Test Small Integer Values
general_skills.principle: When solving equations with exponential terms that resist algebraic manipulation, systematically test small integer values to identify potential solutions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: Equations involving exponential growth/decay terms where algebraic rearrangement is infeasible.

general_skills.title: Analyze Sign and Growth Behavior
general_skills.principle: Compare the sign and growth rates of equation sides to eliminate impossible solution ranges (e.g., negative values or values beyond a critical threshold).
general_skills.when_to_apply: Equations with mixed polynomial/exponential terms where solution ranges can be bounded by sign analysis.

general_skills.title: Logarithmic to Exponential Conversion
general_skills.principle: Reframe logarithmic conditions into exponential equations to uncover integer relationships between variables.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves logarithms with integer outputs and requires integer variable relationships.

general_skills.title: Iterative Exponent Analysis
general_skills.principle: Systematically evaluate integer exponents, compute valid bases via root functions, and aggregate counts while respecting constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When counting pairs (a, b) under exponential relationships with bounded variables.

general_skills.title: Constraint-Driven Iteration Termination
general_skills.principle: Adjust counts by excluding invalid cases (e.g., a=1) and terminate iterations when constraints (e.g., base ≥2) are no longer satisfied.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When iterating over exponents or bases with explicit range limitations.

general_skills.title: Parity Constraints in Prime Sums
general_skills.principle: When analyzing sums of primes, consider parity (even/odd) to eliminate impossible cases, such as using 2 as one of the primes when the sum is even.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with sums of primes or other number-theoretic constraints involving parity.

general_skills.title: Systematic Value Checking
general_skills.principle: Iteratively test candidate values in ascending/descending order to identify valid solutions that satisfy constraints, especially when optimizing for minimal/maximal values.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When searching for extremal values (minimum/maximum) under a fixed relationship or constraint.

general_skills.title: Complementary Pair Optimization
general_skills.principle: For a fixed sum, the minimal value of one variable corresponds to the maximal value of the other, and vice versa, enabling direct computation of required quantities.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When variables are interdependent through a fixed sum or equation, and extremal values are needed.

general_skills.title: Iterative Simplification
general_skills.principle: Break complex expressions into nested subproblems, solving from the innermost layer outward while maintaining operational precedence.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with deeply nested operations or recursive structures requiring sequential evaluation.

general_skills.title: Pattern Recognition in Recurrence
general_skills.principle: Identify repeating structural patterns (e.g., recursive formulas) that allow generalization of intermediate results across layers.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When evaluating expressions with repetitive operations that exhibit consistent transformation rules.

general_skills.title: Express variables in terms of target quantity
general_skills.principle: Rewrite given constraints using the target quantity as a variable to create equations that can be solved systematically.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When direct computation of the target quantity is obstructed by multiple interdependent variables.

general_skills.title: Solve equations through substitution and algebraic manipulation
general_skills.principle: Substitute expressions derived from relationships into a single equation to eliminate variables and isolate the target quantity.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiple variables are linked through proportional or multiplicative relationships.

general_skills.title: Simplify complex expressions via factoring
general_skills.principle: Factor numerators and denominators to identify common terms and reduce computational complexity.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with products of multiple terms that share common factors.

general_skills.title: Translate Proportional Conditions into Equations
general_skills.principle: Convert percentage or ratio-based problem conditions into algebraic equations by equating the modified quantity to its original value multiplied by the specified factor (e.g., 1.1 for 10% increase).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves percentage changes, proportional relationships, or multiplicative comparisons between quantities.

general_skills.title: Solve Equations for Integer Solutions
general_skills.principle: Manipulate equations to isolate variables and identify integer solutions by factoring, substitution, or leveraging divisibility properties.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When seeking integer solutions to equations derived from problem constraints, especially involving fractions or Diophantine-like conditions.

general_skills.title: Validate Solutions Against Coprimality Constraints
general_skills.principle: Check that candidate solutions satisfy coprimality (or other specified) conditions by computing greatest common divisors (GCDs) or applying number-theoretic properties.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solutions must meet number-theoretic constraints like coprimality, primality, or divisibility requirements.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Geometry Modeling
general_skills.principle: Assign coordinates to geometric entities to translate spatial relationships into algebraic equations, enabling systematic computation.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When spatial configurations involve distances, tangents, or symmetry that can be expressed algebraically.

general_skills.title: Tangent Condition Application
general_skills.principle: Use the distance from a point to a line (or circle) to derive equations that enforce tangency constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a figure is tangent to a line or curve, leveraging distance formulas to establish relationships between variables.

general_skills.title: Systematic Decomposition
general_skills.principle: Break complex problems into sequential steps by defining intermediate variables and solving subproblems incrementally.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When tackling multi-part geometric or algebraic problems requiring stepwise construction of relationships.

general_skills.title: Extended Euclidean Algorithm for Inverses
general_skills.principle: Use the Extended Euclidean Algorithm to find integers x and y such that ax + by = gcd(a, b). When a and b are coprime, x is the multiplicative inverse of a modulo b.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When seeking a multiplicative inverse of a number modulo n, and gcd(a, n) = 1.

general_skills.title: Modulo Adjustment for Positive Residues
general_skills.principle: Convert negative residues to the range [0, n) by adding the modulus n until the result is non-negative.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the computed inverse is negative, adjust it to the required range by adding the modulus.

general_skills.title: Verification via Substitution
general_skills.principle: Confirm the correctness of a solution by substituting it back into the original congruence equation.
general_skills.when_to_apply: After computing a potential inverse, verify it satisfies the congruence ax ≡ 1 mod n.

general_skills.title: Inclusion-Exclusion for Overlapping Constraints
general_skills.principle: When multiple constraints require the exclusion of overlapping invalid cases, systematically subtract invalid configurations while adding back over-subtracted overlaps to avoid double-counting.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves ensuring multiple conditions are met and invalid cases overlap in complex ways.

general_skills.title: Subset Enumeration via Function Mapping
general_skills.principle: Model the problem as functions assigning elements (e.g., songs) to subsets (e.g., liked/disliked combinations), then compute total possibilities by raising the number of valid subsets to the power of elements.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem involves distributing elements to categories with specific constraints on subset memberships.

general_skills.title: Constraint Enforcement via Required Subset Presence
general_skills.principle: Ensure all required subsets (e.g., pairs of girls liking a song) are present by subtracting configurations that lack these subsets, using inclusion-exclusion to correct for over-subtraction.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem mandates the existence of at least one element in specific subsets across all cases.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Geometry Modeling
general_skills.principle: Assign coordinates to geometric figures to translate spatial relationships into algebraic equations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves geometric configurations with distance, reflection, or symmetry constraints.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Constraint Translation
general_skills.principle: Convert geometric conditions (e.g., reflections, midpoints, distances) into algebraic equations to derive relationships between variables.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When direct geometric intuition is insufficient, and symbolic manipulation can reveal hidden relationships.

general_skills.title: Domain-Driven Validity Checks
general_skills.principle: Solve equations while explicitly enforcing problem constraints (e.g., inequalities, integer requirements) to filter valid solutions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solutions require satisfying multiple conditions, such as positivity, bounds, or integrality.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Geometry Translation
general_skills.principle: Assign coordinates to geometric elements to convert the problem into algebraic terms, enabling the use of slopes, distances, and equations to represent constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with geometric configurations involving lengths, angles, or slopes.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Condition Application
general_skills.principle: Use algebraic conditions derived from geometric properties (e.g., slopes for perpendicularity) to form equations that encode the problem's constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When given constraints involve geometric relationships like perpendicularity, midpoints, or parallelism.

general_skills.title: Systematic Equation Solving
general_skills.principle: Derive and solve equations systematically to find the target quantity, ensuring consistency with all problem constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem requires finding a numerical value based on algebraic relationships.

general_skills.title: Sequence Approximation via Known Integer Sequences
general_skills.principle: Recognize that a sequence's rounded terms can be expressed as terms of a known integer sequence (e.g., Fibonacci numbers) and substitute into its generating function for summation.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When evaluating sums involving rounded terms of exponential sequences with irrational constants.

general_skills.title: Generating Function Application for Infinite Series
general_skills.principle: Use generating functions of known integer sequences to compute infinite sums by leveraging closed-form expressions or recurrence relations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When summing series with terms that align with coefficients of a generating function for a well-known sequence.

general_skills.title: Constant-Sequence Relationship Exploitation
general_skills.principle: Leverage properties of constants (e.g., golden ratio) to derive exact relationships with integer sequences, enabling term-by-term substitution in sums.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a constant's powers exhibit predictable integer approximations or connections to combinatorial sequences.

general_skills.title: Systematic Case Enumeration
general_skills.principle: Break down the problem by iterating through all possible values of one variable to ensure completeness in counting favorable outcomes.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem involves discrete, finite choices where exhaustive analysis of individual cases is feasible.

general_skills.title: Coprimality Filtering
general_skills.principle: Use the greatest common divisor (GCD) to identify pairs of numbers that are relatively prime, leveraging number theory properties for efficient filtering.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining relationships between numbers where pairwise coprimality is a key condition.

general_skills.title: Aggregation of Partial Results
general_skills.principle: Sum results from individual cases to compute the total number of favorable outcomes, ensuring consistency with the problem's constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving problems requiring cumulative analysis of disjoint subsets of possibilities.

general_skills.title: Interval Case Evaluation
general_skills.principle: Determine the correct case by comparing the input value to interval boundaries defined in the piecewise function.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving problems with piecewise-defined functions or conditional expressions.

general_skills.title: Case-Specific Formula Application
general_skills.principle: Apply the formula or rule corresponding to the identified case once the input's interval membership is confirmed.
general_skills.when_to_apply: After verifying the input satisfies the conditions of a specific case in a piecewise or conditional problem.

general_skills.title: Exclusivity Verification
general_skills.principle: Confirm the input does not satisfy other cases by explicitly checking against remaining interval conditions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: To eliminate ambiguity in piecewise functions or multi-case scenarios.

general_skills.title: Pattern Recognition via Coefficient Structure
general_skills.principle: Identify coefficient patterns (e.g., powers of integers, recursive scaling) that suggest substitutions or factoring to simplify the equation.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When coefficients exhibit structured relationships (e.g., multiples of powers, arithmetic progressions).

general_skills.title: Positive Definite Term Isolation
general_skills.principle: Leverage positive definite expressions (e.g., sums of squares) to isolate and eliminate non-real roots, narrowing the search space for real solutions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the equation contains terms that are always non-negative or non-positive for real inputs.

general_skills.title: Quadratic Substitution for Higher-Degree Equations
general_skills.principle: Transform higher-degree equations into quadratic form via substitution, enabling the use of the quadratic formula to find roots.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the equation can be rewritten as a quadratic in a substituted variable (e.g., $ y = ax^k $).

general_skills.title: Algebraic Simplification via Structured Patterns
general_skills.principle: Rewrite complex expressions as sums of squares or recognizable algebraic forms to expose hidden structure and simplify optimization.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the expression contains symmetric or quadratic terms that can be factored or completed into squares.

general_skills.title: Variable Substitution for Complexity Reduction
general_skills.principle: Introduce substitutions (e.g., z = x²) to transform multi-variable expressions into single-variable problems, reducing computational complexity.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When terms involve powers of variables that can be expressed in terms of a single parameter or symmetric relationship.

general_skills.title: Calculus-Based Critical Point Verification
general_skills.principle: Use partial derivatives to identify and validate critical points in multivariable optimization problems, ensuring algebraic solutions are correct.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When algebraic methods yield potential minima/maxima, and verification of extrema is required.

general_skills.title: Constraint-Based Digit Analysis
general_skills.principle: Identify which digits or digit positions are required to satisfy the problem's numerical range or condition, narrowing the scope of valid cases.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem involves forming numbers with specific ranges or properties, such as determining valid tens or units digits.

general_skills.title: Systematic Case Enumeration
general_skills.principle: Enumerate all valid combinations by considering permutations and constraints, ensuring no overlaps or omissions in counting favorable outcomes.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When outcomes depend on multiple variables (e.g., dice rolls) and order matters, such as forming numbers from distinct elements.

general_skills.title: Probability via Favorable-to-Total Ratio
general_skills.principle: Calculate probability by dividing the number of favorable outcomes by the total possible outcomes, ensuring both are computed accurately under the problem's constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem requires determining likelihood based on discrete, equally probable outcomes.

general_skills.title: Terminating Decimal Condition
general_skills.principle: A fraction has a terminating decimal expansion if and only if its denominator (in reduced form) has no prime factors other than 2 and 5. Use this to characterize valid denominators for terminating decimals.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing decimal expansions of fractions or counting numbers with specific decimal properties.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis via Exponent Constraints
general_skills.principle: Split problems involving exponents (e.g., prime factorizations) into cases based on inequalities between exponents, then solve for valid ranges of variables.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with multiplicative structures (e.g., 2^a * 5^b) and constraints on their magnitudes.

general_skills.title: Digit-Length Categorization
general_skills.principle: Count solutions by partitioning them into categories defined by digit lengths (or other discrete constraints) and summing contributions from each category.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving problems with bounds on numeric size (e.g., numbers less than 10^k) and properties dependent on their magnitude.

general_skills.title: Block-wise Pattern Analysis
general_skills.principle: Divide the problem into segments (e.g., intervals between perfect squares) to identify and simplify the underlying pattern, enabling manageable sub-problems.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a sequence or series exhibits periodic or threshold-based changes in behavior.

general_skills.title: Inductive Generalization
general_skills.principle: Test a conjectured pattern on small cases, then use mathematical induction to prove its validity for all cases, ensuring universal applicability.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a pattern is observed in specific instances and needs to be extended to general cases.

general_skills.title: Leverage Multiplicative Properties
general_skills.principle: Use the multiplicative property of a function to decompose composite numbers into prime factors and compute their function values recursively.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a function is defined as multiplicative (f(mn) = f(m)f(n)) and you need to evaluate it at composite arguments.

general_skills.title: Infer Function Form from Monotonicity
general_skills.principle: Combine strict monotonicity (f(m) < f(n) if m < n) with functional equations to deduce the function's structure (e.g., identity function).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a function is strictly increasing and satisfies a multiplicative or recursive property, use monotonicity to constrain its form.

general_skills.title: Anchor with Given Values
general_skills.principle: Use specific known values (e.g., f(2) = 2) as anchors to iteratively compute other values via functional equations and constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a function's behavior is partially defined, use provided values to bootstrap the solution process.

general_skills.title: Complete the Square for Quadratic Constraints
general_skills.principle: Transform quadratic equations into standard forms (e.g., ellipses, circles) by completing the square to reveal geometric interpretations and simplify constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with quadratic equations or constraints involving multiple variables.

general_skills.title: Recognize and Simplify Algebraic Identities
general_skills.principle: Identify patterns in target expressions (e.g., perfect squares, factored forms) to rewrite them into simpler, more manageable forms that align with constraints or optimization goals.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When tasked with maximizing/minimizing expressions involving symmetric or structured terms.

general_skills.title: Parameterize Constraints for Optimization
general_skills.principle: Use trigonometric or parametric representations (e.g., sine/cosine) to convert conic section constraints into single-variable functions, enabling direct computation of extrema via amplitude analysis or calculus.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When optimizing expressions under quadratic constraints that form closed curves (e.g., ellipses, circles).

general_skills.title: Coordinate Geometry for Regular Polygons
general_skills.principle: Model regular polygons using coordinate systems to calculate vertex positions and derive area relationships through algebraic computation.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves regular polygons and requires precise geometric relationships between vertices or areas.

general_skills.title: Symmetry-Based Area Scaling
general_skills.principle: Leverage symmetry and proportional reasoning to scale areas between different configurations while preserving geometric constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem provides a total area and requires finding the area of a sub-region within a symmetric figure.

general_skills.title: Inscribed Circle Properties
general_skills.principle: Use properties of inscribed circles (e.g., radius, angular spacing) to decompose complex shapes into manageable components for area calculation.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When working with regular polygons or cyclic figures where vertices lie on a common circle.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis by Variable Partitioning
general_skills.principle: Split complex constraints into manageable cases by partitioning variables (e.g., counts of specific elements) across problem segments (e.g., first vs. last three rolls).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiple constraints interact non-linearly, such as product equality and fixed element counts.

general_skills.title: Variable Substitution for Constraint Simplification
general_skills.principle: Introduce variables to represent subsets of the problem (e.g., number of 6s in a segment) to transform constraints into algebraic relationships.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When direct computation of combinatorial counts is infeasible due to overlapping conditions.

general_skills.title: Constraint Validation via Direct Comparison
general_skills.principle: Systematically eliminate invalid cases by comparing derived values against all problem constraints (e.g., product equality, element limits).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When cases involve interdependent conditions that require explicit verification of feasibility.

general_skills.title: Decompose Complex Shapes into Simpler Components
general_skills.principle: Break down complex geometric shapes into simpler, known components (e.g., pyramids, prisms) to compute their volumes or other properties.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When direct volume formulas for a shape are unknown or non-trivial.

general_skills.title: Apply Standard Volume Formulas for Regular Polyhedra
general_skills.principle: Recall and apply established volume formulas for regular polyhedra (e.g., octahedron, cuboctahedron) to compute their volumes directly.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem involves comparing volumes of standard geometric solids with known formulas.

general_skills.title: Simplify Algebraic Ratios
general_skills.principle: Simplify ratios by canceling common terms and performing arithmetic operations to isolate the target quantity.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem requires computing a ratio of quantities expressed algebraically.

general_skills.title: Cyclomatic Number Minimization
general_skills.principle: Use the cyclomatic number formula (m - n + p) to determine the minimum number of cycles by minimizing the number of connected components (p).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When optimizing for the minimal number of cycles in a graph with given vertices and edges.

general_skills.title: Connectedness Assumption
general_skills.principle: Assume the graph is connected to achieve the minimal cyclomatic number, as increasing connected components raises the lower bound on cycles.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When seeking the minimal cycle count, prioritize connectedness to reduce the cyclomatic number.

general_skills.title: Iterative Elimination Pattern Recognition
general_skills.principle: Identify that repeated elimination processes reduce the problem to numbers with a specific congruence property (e.g., multiples of increasing powers of two), enabling prediction of the final survivor through pattern analysis.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves sequential elimination rounds with consistent rules, such as marking every other element in a list.

general_skills.title: Recursive Subproblem Modeling
general_skills.principle: Model the problem as a recurrence relation where each step depends on a smaller subproblem, allowing systematic computation of the solution through recursive decomposition.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem can be broken into smaller, structurally similar subproblems, such as elimination processes with diminishing lists.

general_skills.title: Apply Sum-to-Product Identities
general_skills.principle: Use sum-to-product identities to combine trigonometric terms into products, revealing simplification opportunities through symmetry or cancellation.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with sums of sine or cosine terms with arithmetic progressions or symmetric arguments.

general_skills.title: Leverage Angle Relationships
general_skills.principle: Transform angles using supplementary/complementary identities (e.g., $\sin(\pi - x) = \sin x$) to expose hidden relationships or simplify expressions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When expressions involve angles that sum to $\pi$ or $\frac{\pi}{2}$, or when terms can be rewritten as complementary/supplementary angles.

general_skills.title: Systematic Decomposition
general_skills.principle: Break complex expressions into smaller components by grouping terms, applying identities step-by-step, and iteratively simplifying until a closed-form solution emerges.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with multi-term expressions requiring sequential simplification or when direct evaluation is intractable.

general_skills.title: Modular Congruence for Trailing Digits
general_skills.principle: Translate a requirement for trailing digits (e.g., all 9s) into a congruence relation modulo a power of 10. For example, trailing k 9s implies the number ≡ -1 mod 10^k.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves constraints on the last digits of a number.

general_skills.title: Prime Exponent Calculation via Legendre's Formula
general_skills.principle: Compute the exponent of a prime p in a factorial using Legendre's formula: sum_{i=1}^∞ floor(n/p^i). This is critical for analyzing divisibility by prime powers.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining the divisibility of a factorial or product by a prime power.

general_skills.title: Aggregate Prime Contributions in Products
general_skills.principle: Decompose a complex product into its components, calculate the required prime exponents for each part, and sum them to verify overall divisibility by a composite modulus (e.g., 10^k = 2^k * 5^k).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing the divisibility of a product of multiple terms by a composite number.

general_skills.title: Decompose into Trigonometric Components
general_skills.principle: Break down the target quantity (e.g., area) into additive trigonometric terms that can be maximized independently, leveraging identities like sine and cosine laws for cyclic polygons.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When optimizing areas or lengths in cyclic polygons with angular constraints.

general_skills.title: Symmetry-Driven Optimization
general_skills.principle: Assume symmetric configurations for variables under optimization constraints to simplify calculations, particularly when sums of trigonometric functions are involved.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When maximizing sums of periodic functions under symmetric or constrained conditions.

general_skills.title: Leverage Known Trigonometric Maxima
general_skills.principle: Apply the fact that sine and cosine functions attain their maxima at specific angles (e.g., sinθ ≤ 1, cosθ ≤ 1) to determine optimal angular configurations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When optimizing expressions involving trigonometric functions with bounded ranges.

general_skills.title: Modular Candidate Generation
general_skills.principle: Generate numbers that satisfy a modular condition by iterating through arithmetic progressions defined by the congruence relation.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem requires selecting numbers that fit a specific modular arithmetic constraint.

general_skills.title: Systematic Primality Filtering
general_skills.principle: Filter candidates by verifying primality through exhaustive divisibility checks against known primes or factorization.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When eliminating non-prime numbers from a list of candidates generated by a mathematical condition.

general_skills.title: Decomposition for Accurate Summation
general_skills.principle: Break complex summations into smaller, sequential additions to minimize computational errors and improve manageability.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When summing large sets of numbers to ensure accuracy and reduce cognitive load.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Geometry Modeling
general_skills.principle: Represent geometric configurations with coordinates to translate spatial relationships into algebraic equations, enabling systematic analysis.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When spatial relationships involve circles, tangents, or distances that can be expressed numerically.

general_skills.title: Tangent Condition Application
general_skills.principle: Use the distance between centers of tangent circles (sum/difference of radii) to establish equations governing their positions and sizes.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When circles are tangent (externally or internally) and their centers' distances relate to radii.

general_skills.title: Systematic Equation Solving
general_skills.principle: Derive and solve systems of equations from geometric constraints to determine unknown quantities, prioritizing algebraic simplification and case analysis.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiple interdependent relationships exist between variables in a geometric or combinatorial problem.

general_skills.title: State Decomposition with Constraints
general_skills.principle: Break the problem into states that capture all necessary information (e.g., current progress, last action) and constraints, enabling systematic analysis of transitions and probabilities.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem involves sequential decisions with conditional restrictions or dependencies on prior states.

general_skills.title: Recursive Expectation Equations
general_skills.principle: Express the target quantity as a combination of expected values from subsequent states, forming a system of equations solvable through substitution or linear algebra.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When calculating expected values in stochastic processes with multiple states and transitions.

general_skills.title: Constraint-Driven Transition Modeling
general_skills.principle: Adjust transition probabilities or validity based on problem-specific constraints, ensuring the model adheres to rules that invalidate certain paths.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When transitions are restricted by conditions that eliminate specific outcomes or states.

general_skills.title: Square Absolute Values
general_skills.principle: Square both sides of an absolute value inequality to eliminate them, ensuring the resulting equation is equivalent by considering the domain of the original inequality.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When comparing absolute values of expressions involving polynomials or algebraic terms.

general_skills.title: Simplify Polynomial Expressions
general_skills.principle: Transform complex polynomial inequalities by expanding, combining like terms, and eliminating fractions through multiplication by a common denominator.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with inequalities involving rational or fractional polynomial terms.

general_skills.title: Analyze Polynomial Sign Changes
general_skills.principle: Solve polynomial inequalities by identifying critical points (roots) and testing intervals to determine where the inequality holds, leveraging the polynomial's leading coefficient and root behavior.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving inequalities involving higher-degree polynomials with real roots.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Transformation for Factorable Equations
general_skills.principle: When solving for variables in a problem involving counts or interactions, manipulate the equation to reveal a factorable form, enabling the identification of integer solutions through factor pairs.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When an equation can be transformed into a product of terms that aligns with problem constraints, such as handshake counts in grid structures.

general_skills.title: Constraint-Driven Solution Validation
general_skills.principle: After generating potential solutions, systematically eliminate those that violate given constraints, ensuring all variables meet the problem's minimum or other specified conditions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiple solutions exist, validate each against explicit constraints (e.g., m, n ≥ 3) to identify valid configurations.

general_skills.title: Leverage Symmetry
general_skills.principle: Assume symmetric configurations when constraints imply mirrored structures, reducing variables and simplifying calculations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves symmetric elements (e.g., axes, shapes) or mirrored constraints.

general_skills.title: Apply Geometric Constraints Algebraically
general_skills.principle: Substitute coordinates of points into given geometric equations (e.g., ellipse, circle) to derive relationships between variables.
