general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem provides explicit geometric constraints that can be translated into algebraic equations.

general_skills.title: Use Figure Properties for Equations
general_skills.principle: Derive equations based on intrinsic properties of the figure (e.g., equilateral triangle side lengths, angles) to relate coordinates.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem involves specific geometric figures with definable properties (e.g., equal sides, angles).

general_skills.title: Geometric Probability Modeling
general_skills.principle: Represent variables as coordinates in a geometric space to calculate probabilities via area ratios.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with continuous uniform distributions over two variables and overlapping conditions.

general_skills.title: Area Subtraction for Favorable Outcomes
general_skills.principle: Compute the probability by subtracting non-overlapping regions' areas from the total area in geometric models.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining the likelihood of overlapping events in continuous time or space intervals.

general_skills.title: Fraction Simplification via GCD
general_skills.principle: Reduce fractions to lowest terms by factoring numerator and denominator and dividing by their greatest common divisor.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When simplifying rational expressions or probabilities to ensure irreducibility.

general_skills.title: Apply Geometric Theorems
general_skills.principle: Recall and apply established formulas that relate triangle centers (e.g., circumcenter, orthocenter) to side lengths and circumradius.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem involves triangle centers and requires connecting them to side lengths or radii.

general_skills.title: Substitute Values into Algebraic Expressions
general_skills.principle: Plug given numerical values into algebraic formulas derived from geometric relationships to compute the target quantity.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When numerical values for parameters (e.g., side lengths, radii) are provided and a formula exists to relate them to the desired output.

general_skills.title: Geometric Configuration Analysis
general_skills.principle: Identify that a triangle contains the center of a circle if and only if its vertices are not all contained within any semicircle. This principle applies to regular polygons and circle-based problems where central containment depends on arc distribution.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining whether a polygonal configuration (e.g., triangle) contains the center of its circumscribed circle.

general_skills.title: Combinatorial Counting with Overlap Adjustment
general_skills.principle: Calculate the number of invalid configurations (e.g., triangles within a semicircle) by fixing a starting point, enumerating valid pairs, and adjusting for overcounting using rotational symmetry or known combinatorial formulas.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When counting configurations in symmetric structures (e.g., regular polygons) where overlapping cases must be systematically accounted for.

general_skills.title: Trigonometric Constraint Simplification
general_skills.principle: Use trigonometric identities and angle sum properties to simplify equations involving triangle angles, deriving constraints on angle measures.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When given a trigonometric equation involving triangle angles, express angles in terms of a single variable using the triangle angle sum and simplify.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis for Optimal Configurations
general_skills.principle: Evaluate different geometric configurations (e.g., angle positions) to determine the maximum or minimum value of a quantity, eliminating invalid cases based on constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When optimizing a length or value in a geometric problem with multiple valid configurations, systematically analyze each case to identify the optimal solution.

general_skills.title: Law of Cosines for Length Calculation
general_skills.principle: Apply the Law of Cosines to compute side lengths when an angle is known, considering how angle placement affects the result.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When calculating side lengths in a triangle with a known angle, use the Law of Cosines and prioritize configurations that maximize or minimize the desired length.

general_skills.title: Segment Ratio Division
general_skills.principle: Use the section formula to find coordinates of a point dividing a segment in a given ratio, preserving proportional relationships between coordinates.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem requires locating a point that divides a line segment between two known points in a specific ratio.

general_skills.title: Horizontal Line Intersection
general_skills.principle: A horizontal line through a point on a curve has a constant y-value, which can be equated to the function's value to find intersection points.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a horizontal line intersects a curve, set the y-coordinate of the line equal to the function's value and solve for x.

general_skills.title: Logarithmic Equation Solving
general_skills.principle: Solve equations involving logarithms by exponentiating both sides to isolate the variable, leveraging the inverse relationship between logarithmic and exponential functions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When an equation contains a logarithm, apply exponentiation to both sides to transform it into a solvable algebraic form.

general_skills.title: Subset Union Constraint
general_skills.principle: Ensure the entire set is a subset of the union of the required number types (e.g., Fibonacci and triangular numbers) to enable partitioning into disjoint subsets with specific properties.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem requires partitioning a set into subsets defined by distinct number sequences or categories.

general_skills.title: Minimum Size Verification
general_skills.principle: Check that the set size meets the minimum requirement for partitioning (e.g., at least four elements for two subsets of size ≥2 each).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When partitioning into multiple subsets with size constraints is required.

general_skills.title: Consecutive Sequence Validation
general_skills.principle: Verify that elements can be grouped into consecutive sequences of the required type (e.g., Fibonacci or triangular numbers) within the subsets.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When subsets must consist of consecutive elements from a specific number sequence.

general_skills.title: Formulate Equations from Constraints
general_skills.principle: Translate problem conditions into mathematical equations using standard formulas (e.g., sum of geometric series, nth term formula) to create a system of equations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When given relationships between variables (e.g., equal sums, specific term values) and need to derive equations for solving.

general_skills.title: Solve Systems via Algebraic Manipulation
general_skills.principle: Solve for unknowns by manipulating equations through substitution, factoring, or simplification, ensuring consistency with constraints like |r| < 1 for geometric series.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiple equations involve variables requiring elimination or substitution to isolate unknowns.

general_skills.title: Rationalize Expressions with Radicals
general_skills.principle: Eliminate radicals from denominators by multiplying numerator and denominator by conjugates, simplifying to express results in standard forms (e.g., m + √n).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When final answers require rationalized forms or specific radical expressions to match problem requirements.

general_skills.title: Case-Based Constraint Analysis
general_skills.principle: Break down complex divisibility conditions into distinct cases based on problem constraints, then validate each case's implications for the solution.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with multi-condition problems requiring verification across ranges of values (e.g., m ≤ n).

general_skills.title: Algebraic Simplification via Factoring
general_skills.principle: Factor and cancel common terms in expressions to reveal underlying multiplicative relationships, especially when comparing large quantities.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When simplifying ratios or products involving large numbers with shared factors.

general_skills.title: Negligible Term Approximation
general_skills.principle: Approximate ratios by ignoring small terms when their contribution is less than the required precision (e.g., ±0.5 for nearest-integer problems).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When final answers require integer approximation and minor terms have minimal impact on the result.

general_skills.title: GCD Difference Reduction
general_skills.principle: The greatest common divisor of two numbers also divides their difference. Use this to reduce complex expressions to simpler forms by subtracting them.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When comparing large numbers or expressions whose direct computation is infeasible.

general_skills.title: Difference of Squares Factorization
general_skills.principle: Express squared terms as differences of squares to factor them into linear components, simplifying arithmetic operations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with squared terms in algebraic expressions requiring simplification or modular analysis.

general_skills.title: Prime Factor Divisibility Testing
general_skills.principle: Identify potential divisors of a number by testing its prime factors, then verify divisibility of the original expressions using modular arithmetic.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When narrowing down possible greatest common divisors after reducing the problem to a smaller candidate set.

general_skills.title: Leverage Logarithmic Identities
general_skills.principle: Convert sums of logarithms into products using the identity $\log_b x + \log_b y = \log_b (xy)$, simplifying complex expressions into manageable forms.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When encountering sums of logarithms with the same base in an equation.

general_skills.title: Transform to Exponential Form
general_skills.principle: Convert logarithmic equations to their exponential equivalents to expose hidden constraints and relationships between variables.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving equations involving logarithms and seeking to relate variables through exponentiation.

general_skills.title: Parameterize Variables via Common Bases
general_skills.principle: Express variables as powers of a shared base (e.g., 2) to decompose exponential equations into linear constraints, enabling systematic enumeration of integer solutions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with exponential equations requiring integer solutions and a clear common base exists.

general_skills.title: Avoid Palindromic Substrings via Structural Patterns
general_skills.principle: Construct permutations with alternating or non-repeating patterns to inherently prevent palindromic substrings by ensuring no two identical letters are adjacent and avoiding symmetric sequences.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When constraints require eliminating palindromic substrings of length ≥2, especially in permutations with repeated elements.

general_skills.title: Calculate Permutations with Repeated Elements
general_skills.principle: Compute total permutations by dividing the factorial of the total elements by the product of the factorials of the counts of each repeated element.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining the total number of distinct arrangements of a multiset.

general_skills.title: Leverage Nested Palindrome Properties
general_skills.principle: Focus on eliminating smaller palindromic substrings first, as longer palindromes inherently contain shorter ones, simplifying constraint enforcement.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing palindromic substrings in sequences, prioritize eliminating smaller-length substrings to cover longer cases.

general_skills.title: Leverage Sequence Properties
general_skills.principle: Express variables in terms of a common difference or ratio to exploit structural relationships in sequences.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When variables form an arithmetic or geometric progression, or when symmetry exists in the problem.

general_skills.title: Substitute Constraints to Simplify
general_skills.principle: Replace complex relationships with simplified equations by substituting derived constraints into the main problem.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiple constraints (e.g., perimeter, sequence conditions) exist and can be combined algebraically.

general_skills.title: Validate via Inequalities
general_skills.principle: Ensure solutions satisfy all necessary conditions (e.g., triangle inequality) and eliminate degenerate or invalid cases.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When verifying the feasibility of candidate solutions or ensuring distinctness/validity.

general_skills.title: Interval Partitioning
general_skills.principle: Partition the domain into intervals where the function's value is constant by analyzing its definition and solving for boundary conditions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a function's output depends on ranges of input values, such as proximity to thresholds or piecewise definitions.

general_skills.title: Boundary Inequality Solving
general_skills.principle: Use the function's definition to derive and solve inequalities that determine the exact start and end of intervals where the function's value remains constant.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the function's behavior is defined by mathematical thresholds or proximity conditions.

general_skills.title: Contribution Aggregation
general_skills.principle: Compute the total by summing contributions from each interval, calculated as (number of elements in interval) × (reciprocal of the function's value on that interval).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When summing over a domain partitioned into intervals with constant function values.

general_skills.title: Modular Arithmetic Translation
general_skills.principle: When two expressions have the same remainder modulo a divisor, their difference is divisible by that divisor. Use this to set up an equation involving divisibility.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When comparing remainders of two expressions under a common divisor.

general_skills.title: Divisor-Based Solution Search
general_skills.principle: To find the minimal solution, identify the smallest divisor of a number that satisfies a constraint (e.g., being larger than a given value) and compute the variable accordingly.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving for a variable constrained by a divisor relationship requiring minimal value.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis by Variable Properties
general_skills.principle: Split the problem into distinct cases based on the properties of variables (e.g., sign, integer status) to isolate different behaviors of functions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with functions involving piecewise definitions, absolute values, or floor/ceiling operations that exhibit different behaviors under varying conditions.

general_skills.title: Component Decomposition
general_skills.principle: Break complex expressions into their constituent parts to analyze how each component contributes to the overall function's behavior.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When encountering multi-layered functions (e.g., nested operations, absolute values, or floor functions) that require understanding individual component interactions.

general_skills.title: Property-Based Simplification
general_skills.principle: Leverage known mathematical properties (e.g., floor function behavior, absolute value identities) to reduce expressions to simpler forms or identify invariant patterns.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When simplifying expressions involving standard functions with well-defined properties, such as floor, absolute value, or modular arithmetic.

general_skills.title: Leverage Symmetry to Reduce Complexity
general_skills.principle: Fix one variable (e.g., position of a point on a circle) to exploit symmetry, simplifying the problem while preserving generality.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with uniform distributions on symmetric domains (e.g., circles, spheres).

general_skills.title: Model Probability as a Function of a Variable
general_skills.principle: Express the target probability as a function of the variable of interest (e.g., distance, angle) and solve for the threshold where the condition is met.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When comparing probabilistic outcomes to a threshold involving continuous variables.

general_skills.title: Use Trigonometric Relationships for Geometric Quantities
general_skills.principle: Relate geometric quantities (e.g., chord length, arc length) to trigonometric functions of angles to derive structural equations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing distances or angles in circular or rotational contexts.

general_skills.title: Modular Reduction for Targeted Computation
general_skills.principle: When solving for specific digits of a large number, compute the number modulo a power of ten to isolate the required digits directly.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem requires specific digits (e.g., last three digits) of a large exponentiation.

general_skills.title: Chinese Remainder Theorem Decomposition
general_skills.principle: Decompose a modulus into coprime factors, solve congruences separately, and combine results using the Chinese Remainder Theorem.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the modulus can be factored into pairwise coprime components, enabling independent computation of remainders.

general_skills.title: Pattern Recognition in Modular Exponentiation
general_skills.principle: Identify repeating cycles or periodic patterns in modular exponentiation to simplify large exponent calculations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When exponents are large and modular arithmetic reveals a repeating sequence in powers of a base.

general_skills.title: Greedy Construction with Adjacency Checks
general_skills.principle: When constructing extremal numbers (maximum or minimum) under adjacency constraints, prioritize the largest/smallest available digit at each step while ensuring the next digit does not create a consecutive pair with the previous one.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When generating permutations with specific adjacency restrictions, such as avoiding consecutive digits.

general_skills.title: Iterative Constraint Enforcement
general_skills.principle: At each step of constructing a number, verify that the selected digit adheres to all constraints, particularly adjacency rules, to maintain validity throughout the construction process.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When generating sequences or permutations with explicit constraints on adjacent elements.

general_skills.title: Constraint-Driven Construction
general_skills.principle: Construct sets that satisfy problem constraints by explicitly including required elements and excluding elements that would violate minimality conditions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem requires ensuring a set meets specific criteria while preventing substructures from independently satisfying those criteria.

general_skills.title: Combinatorial Enumeration with Constraints
general_skills.principle: Count valid configurations by selecting elements from restricted ranges, using binomial coefficients to quantify choices while respecting size and inclusion constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When counting subsets with size-dependent properties that require element-specific inclusion/exclusion rules.

general_skills.title: Case-Based Decomposition
general_skills.principle: Break problems into cases based on a parameter (e.g., subset size) and sum results across valid cases, discarding invalid cases where constraints cannot be satisfied.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a solution requires analyzing distinct scenarios defined by discrete parameters with varying constraint validity ranges.

general_skills.title: Model Cyclic Patterns with Modular Arithmetic
general_skills.principle: Use modular arithmetic to track day-of-week shifts between dates, leveraging the 7-day cycle to compute relative positions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving problems involving recurring cycles (e.g., days of the week, calendar dates).

general_skills.title: Account for Variable Day Shifts
general_skills.principle: Adjust calculations for variable day-of-week shifts caused by differing year types (e.g., leap years) to maintain consistency across time intervals.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining dates across years with irregular day counts (e.g., leap years).

general_skills.title: Decompose Sequential Date Calculations
general_skills.principle: Break down complex date problems into sequential steps, using known starting points to compute target dates through incremental reasoning.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When mapping relationships between dates requires stepwise deduction of day-of-week positions.

general_skills.title: Identify Sequence Parameters
general_skills.principle: Determine the first term and common difference by analyzing consecutive terms in an arithmetic sequence.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When given an arithmetic sequence, extract its initial term and the constant difference between terms.

general_skills.title: Apply Nth Term Formula
general_skills.principle: Use the general formula $ a_n = a_1 + (n-1)d $ to find the position of a specific term in an arithmetic sequence.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving for the term number $ n $ corresponding to a given value in an arithmetic sequence.

general_skills.title: Solve and Interpret Equations
general_skills.principle: Solve linear equations derived from sequence properties and adjust results to align with the problem's contextual requirements (e.g., counting terms before a specific value).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When translating sequence relationships into algebraic equations and interpreting the solution within the problem's constraints.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Geometry Modeling
general_skills.principle: Represent geometric figures using coordinate systems to translate spatial relationships into algebraic equations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing spatial configurations involving points, lines, or solids.

general_skills.title: Parameterization of Points on Segments
general_skills.principle: Express positions of points along segments using parameters to capture proportional distances from endpoints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When points are constrained to lie on edges or lines of a figure.

general_skills.title: Distance Equivalence for Regularity
general_skills.principle: Enforce regularity conditions by equating distances between points and solving resulting equations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When ensuring equal edge lengths or symmetry in geometric figures.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Geometry Translation
general_skills.principle: Model geometric problems using coordinate systems to convert spatial relationships into algebraic equations, enabling precise calculations of distances and areas.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When geometric constraints involve distances, regions, or shapes that can be represented with coordinates.

general_skills.title: Distance Constraints as Algebraic Bounds
general_skills.principle: Translate geometric distance conditions (e.g., distance from a line) into algebraic inequalities, defining regions through coordinate-based bounds.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving problems involving regions bounded by distance thresholds from lines or curves.

general_skills.title: Area Decomposition via Subtraction
general_skills.principle: Calculate complex areas by subtracting the area of known sub-regions (e.g., triangles) from larger, simpler regions (e.g., strips or rectangles) defined by constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the target region can be expressed as the difference between a larger region and a subtracted sub-region.

general_skills.title: Track Increment Thresholds
general_skills.principle: Identify points where a function's value changes (e.g., floor(sqrt(a_n)) increasing at perfect squares) and segment the problem into intervals with constant behavior to simplify computation.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a sequence's increment depends on a function that changes at specific thresholds (e.g., floor, ceiling, or piecewise-defined functions).

general_skills.title: Iterative Term Computation
general_skills.principle: Compute terms step-by-step while monitoring how the increment evolves, ensuring precise tracking of progression toward the target value.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving recursive sequences or problems requiring sequential evaluation with dynamic increments based on current state.

general_skills.title: Modular Exponent Analysis
general_skills.principle: When radicals appear in binomial expansions, determine when their exponents yield rational numbers by enforcing modular conditions on the exponents.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When coefficients involve radicals with integer exponents, set up congruence equations to ensure the exponents make the radicals rational.

general_skills.title: Systematic Congruence Solving
general_skills.principle: Solve systems of congruences by combining modular constraints using the Chinese Remainder Theorem or iterative substitution to find valid exponent ranges.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiple modular conditions must be satisfied simultaneously, merge them into a single congruence relation to identify valid parameter values.

general_skills.title: Arithmetic Sequence Counting
general_skills.principle: Count valid terms by identifying arithmetic sequences formed by solutions to congruences and applying the formula for sequence length.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solutions to congruences form an arithmetic progression, calculate the number of terms using the first and last terms and common difference.

general_skills.title: Equation from Average
general_skills.principle: When given an average value, express total quantity as average multiplied by count (total = average × number of items).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When problems involve averages of discrete items with unknown quantities.

general_skills.title: Integer Constraint Testing
general_skills.principle: For problems requiring whole-number solutions, test integer values that satisfy derived equations while respecting problem constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When variables represent discrete entities (e.g., coins, objects) and solutions must be integers.

general_skills.title: Systematic Substitution
general_skills.principle: Substitute simplified expressions into complex equations to reduce variables and isolate target quantities step-by-step.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving systems of equations with multiple variables and interdependent relationships.

general_skills.title: Order Invariance in Multiplicative Sequences
general_skills.principle: The order of applying multiplicative factors (e.g., percentage changes) does not affect the final result due to the commutative property of multiplication. This allows simplifying complex sequences by rearranging operations without altering the outcome.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When evaluating sequences of percentage changes or multiplicative transformations with the same factors applied in different orders.

general_skills.title: Symmetric Sum Simplification
general_skills.principle: Express higher-degree symmetric terms (e.g., x³ + y³) using identities in terms of lower-degree symmetric sums (e.g., x + y and xy) to reduce complexity.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with expressions involving symmetric variables under constraints like x + y = c.

general_skills.title: Constraint-Driven Substitution
general_skills.principle: Substitute variables using given constraints (e.g., y = 3 - x) to transform multi-variable expressions into single-variable functions for optimization.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem has a constraint that relates variables, use it to eliminate variables and simplify the target expression.

general_skills.title: Quadratic Optimization via Vertex Formula
general_skills.principle: Recognize when an expression can be rewritten as a quadratic in a single variable, then apply the vertex formula to find maxima/minima directly.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the target expression reduces to a quadratic form in one variable, use the vertex formula for efficient optimization.

general_skills.title: Modular Congruence from Fractional Parts
general_skills.principle: If two numbers have equal fractional parts when divided by a modulus, their difference is divisible by that modulus. Use this to derive congruences between exponential expressions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When comparing fractional parts of expressions involving exponents and a common denominator.

general_skills.title: Decompose Modulus via Chinese Remainder Theorem
general_skills.principle: Factor composite moduli into coprime components (e.g., powers of primes), solve congruences separately, and combine results using the least common multiple of individual orders.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing periodicity or divisibility properties of exponential functions modulo composite numbers.

general_skills.title: Geometric Constraint Validation
general_skills.principle: After determining candidate values, systematically verify all triangle inequalities to ensure the sides form a valid triangle.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When optimizing quantities under geometric constraints like triangle inequalities or polygonal conditions.

general_skills.title: Domain Restrictions Management
general_skills.principle: Identify and enforce domain restrictions early to eliminate invalid solutions, such as values that cause division by zero or violate given constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving equations with denominators or variables in denominators, or when constraints like |a| ≠ |b| are provided.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Simplification via Term Combination
general_skills.principle: Combine like terms and factor expressions to reduce complex equations to simpler forms, such as quadratics, enabling systematic solution extraction.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with equations involving multiple fractions or symmetric structures that can be simplified through common denominators or factoring.

general_skills.title: Constraint-Driven Case Analysis
general_skills.principle: Split the problem into cases based on given constraints (e.g., |a| ≠ |b|) to explore all valid solution possibilities and ensure distinctness.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When constraints imply relationships between variables (e.g., inequalities or non-zero conditions) that affect solution validity or uniqueness.

general_skills.title: Trigonometric Identity Application
general_skills.principle: Use trigonometric identities (e.g., tangent addition formula) to relate angles and their ratios when angles are decomposed into components.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When given the tangent of a compound angle and information about its component angles or sides.

general_skills.title: Variable Substitution for Unknowns
general_skills.principle: Introduce variables for unknown lengths or quantities and derive equations based on geometric constraints and given ratios.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When direct computation of unknowns is obstructed by multiple interdependent relationships.

general_skills.title: Geometric Decomposition into Right Triangles
general_skills.principle: Break down complex figures into right triangles to leverage Pythagorean theorem and trigonometric ratios for calculations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with altitudes, angles, or segments that create right triangles within a larger geometric configuration.

general_skills.title: Symmetry Exploitation
general_skills.principle: Group terms to reveal hidden symmetry or structure, such as pairing factors in polynomials to simplify the expression into a more tractable form.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with products of linear terms or expressions with consecutive variables.

general_skills.title: Quadratic Optimization
general_skills.principle: Transform the problem into a quadratic form and apply vertex formula or calculus to find minima/maxima, leveraging the known properties of parabolas.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the expression can be reduced to a quadratic or similar standard form with a clear extremum.

general_skills.title: Feasibility Verification
general_skills.principle: Confirm that critical points (e.g., solutions to equations derived from optimization) are achievable by solving the corresponding equations and checking for real roots.
general_skills.when_to_apply: After identifying potential extrema, to ensure the solution corresponds to valid input values.

general_skills.title: Recursive Function Analysis
general_skills.principle: Model recursive functions by identifying the next base case and calculating steps to reach it, using the function's definition to express values in terms of perfect squares or other terminating conditions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When encountering recursive definitions with conditional base cases and incremental steps toward a terminating condition.

general_skills.title: Parity-Driven Constraints
general_skills.principle: Account for parity constraints when defining recursive steps that increment by a fixed step size, ensuring the next valid base case matches the required parity (even/odd) for consistency.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When recursive functions involve stepwise increments that affect parity or other properties of the input.

general_skills.title: Equation Formulation with Constraints
general_skills.principle: Formulate and solve equations derived from recursive definitions, incorporating constraints like parity and base case conditions to narrow valid solutions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving for variables in problems involving recursive relations with multiple constraints.

general_skills.title: Equal Contribution Modeling
general_skills.principle: When multiple entities contribute equal amounts to a recipient, assign a variable to represent the common contribution and express each entity's original amount as a multiple of this variable based on the given fractional relationships.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves equal monetary transfers from different sources with fractional relationships to the recipient.

general_skills.title: Total Amount Calculation
general_skills.principle: Sum all original amounts (including the recipient's initial holdings) and the recipient's new holdings to compute the total pool of money in the system.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining the total quantity in a system where values are distributed or transferred among entities.

general_skills.title: Fractional Share Determination
general_skills.principle: Calculate the fractional share of the recipient by dividing their new holdings by the total pool of money, simplifying the resulting fraction to its lowest terms.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When evaluating the proportion of a quantity that a specific entity possesses relative to the entire system.

general_skills.title: Prime Factorization via Legendre's Formula
general_skills.principle: Compute exponents in a number's prime factorization by summing floor(n/p^k) for each prime p and integer k ≥ 1 until p^k > n.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining the prime factorization of a factorial or any number, especially when analyzing divisors or roots.

general_skills.title: Exponent Adjustment for Perfect Squares
general_skills.principle: For the largest perfect square divisor, adjust each exponent in the prime factorization to the nearest lower even number by taking floor(exponent / 2) * 2.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When identifying the largest perfect square divisor of a number with a known prime factorization.

general_skills.title: Exponent Halving for Square Roots
general_skills.principle: To compute the square root of a number with a known prime factorization, divide each exponent by 2.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When taking the square root of a number expressed in its prime factorized form.

general_skills.title: Vector Parity Modeling
general_skills.principle: Represent numbers as vectors in GF(2) based on the parity of prime exponents to identify groupings that form perfect squares. This allows transforming multiplicative constraints into additive vector equations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem requires balancing exponents in prime factorizations to satisfy multiplicative properties like perfect squares.

general_skills.title: Decomposition by Known Structures
general_skills.principle: Separate elements into categories with known properties (e.g., perfect squares) and focus vector analysis on the remaining elements to simplify partitioning.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem contains elements that inherently satisfy the target condition, isolate them to reduce complexity in the remaining partitioning task.

general_skills.title: Total Vector Balancing
general_skills.principle: Calculate the aggregate vector of all elements to determine necessary groupings that cancel out odd exponents, ensuring the entire set can be partitioned into valid groups.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the total vector of elements indicates an imbalance that must be resolved by forming specific groups to achieve the desired multiplicative property.

general_skills.title: Leverage Number-Theoretic Structures
general_skills.principle: Recognize when problem constraints align with known mathematical structures (e.g., Pythagorean triples) to simplify the search space.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When variables satisfy algebraic relationships that correspond to classical number-theoretic or geometric constructs.

general_skills.title: Systematic Enumeration Under Constraints
general_skills.principle: Iterate through bounded possibilities (e.g., single-digit values) while maintaining consistency with problem constraints to identify valid candidates.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the solution space is discrete and limited by explicit bounds or digit/variable ranges.

general_skills.title: Prime Factorization for Extremal Analysis
general_skills.principle: Decompose candidate solutions into prime factors to identify extremal values (e.g., largest/smallest prime factors) directly.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the goal requires analyzing multiplicative properties or extremal values of numbers.

general_skills.title: Model Temporal Relationships
general_skills.principle: Introduce variables for distinct time points (past, present, future) and express their relationships through equations based on the problem's timeline.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem involves comparisons between ages or quantities at different times.

general_skills.title: Translate Relational Statements into Equations
general_skills.principle: Convert complex verbal relationships (e.g., 'twice as old as', 'seven years from') into algebraic equations by identifying key variables and their dependencies.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem contains multi-step relational descriptions requiring symbolic representation.

general_skills.title: Solve Systems via Substitution
general_skills.principle: Simplify equations by substituting expressions for variables, eliminating redundant terms, and isolating the target quantity through algebraic manipulation.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving for an unknown in a system of equations with overlapping variables.

general_skills.title: Linearity of Expectation
general_skills.principle: Calculate expected values by summing individual probabilities of events, even when events are dependent, by treating each element independently.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem involves counting or measuring an aggregate quantity with probabilistic components.

general_skills.title: Range-Based Case Analysis
general_skills.principle: Split complex counting problems into cases based on value ranges or structural properties to simplify enumeration and avoid overcounting.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When direct counting is infeasible, and the problem can be partitioned into disjoint, manageable subproblems.

general_skills.title: Symmetric Pair Enumeration
general_skills.principle: Count valid pairs by iterating through each element and determining its valid counterparts, leveraging symmetry or constraints to avoid redundant calculations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem involves pairs with specific difference or relation constraints, such as label differences or geometric properties.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis for Tangency Configurations
general_skills.principle: Identify and evaluate distinct geometric configurations (e.g., external/ internal tangency) that satisfy the problem's constraints, as different configurations yield distinct solutions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiple geometric possibilities exist for tangency or intersection conditions.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Modeling of Geometric Constraints
general_skills.principle: Translate geometric relationships (e.g., distance between centers, tangency conditions) into algebraic equations and solve the system to find candidate solutions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem requires combining geometric properties with algebraic computation to derive precise results.

general_skills.title: Validation of Solution Feasibility
general_skills.principle: Filter out invalid solutions by verifying they meet all problem-specific criteria (e.g., positive radii, correct tangency, point inclusion).
general_skills.when_to_apply: After generating candidate solutions, to ensure they are mathematically valid and contextually appropriate.

general_skills.title: Factor with Algebraic Identities
general_skills.principle: Factor expressions using standard algebraic identities (e.g., difference of cubes, sum of cubes) to reveal hidden structure and simplify terms.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When encountering polynomials that can be factored into simpler components, such as differences or sums of powers.

general_skills.title: Telescope Products via Cancellation
general_skills.principle: Decompose products into parts that allow intermediate terms to cancel, often by splitting fractions into sequential factors that align for telescoping.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When evaluating infinite products or sums where terms can be expressed as ratios of sequential components.

general_skills.title: Limit Simplified Partial Products
general_skills.principle: Analyze the behavior of partial products as their upper bound approaches infinity, simplifying expressions to extract the finite limit.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining convergence of infinite products by reducing them to manageable algebraic forms.

general_skills.title: Segment by Digit Length
general_skills.principle: Decompose the problem into segments based on the number of digits in the numbers (e.g., single-digit, two-digit) to compute cumulative digit counts efficiently.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with sequences where numbers contribute varying digit lengths (e.g., 1-digit vs. 2-digit numbers).

general_skills.title: Locate Target via Cumulative Sums
general_skills.principle: Use cumulative sums of digit contributions to identify the exact range (e.g., specific number) where the target digit falls.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the target position requires narrowing down to a specific number or group of numbers in a sequence.

general_skills.title: Analyze Repeated Digit Patterns
general_skills.principle: Determine the exact digit by analyzing the repeating pattern of the identified number's digits (e.g., alternating sequences).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the target digit lies within a repeated sequence of a number's digits (e.g., writing a number multiple times).

general_skills.title: Vieta's Symmetric Sum Mapping
general_skills.principle: Map polynomial coefficients to symmetric sums of roots using Vieta's formulas to establish relationships between coefficients and root properties.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a polynomial's coefficients are linked to sums/products of roots, and constraints on roots are given.

general_skills.title: AM-GM Optimization with Constraints
general_skills.principle: Apply the AM-GM inequality to optimize sums or products under constraints, leveraging equality conditions for extremal values.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When optimizing a symmetric function of variables with fixed sum and product constraints.

general_skills.title: Equality Case Leveraging
general_skills.principle: Assume equality among variables when optimizing under symmetric constraints to identify extremal configurations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When an inequality's equality condition (e.g., AM-GM) aligns with the problem's symmetry or constraints.

general_skills.title: Arithmetic Sequence Recognition
general_skills.principle: When a problem involves a condition where one element is the average of two others, recognize that the elements form an arithmetic sequence. This allows leveraging sequence properties to simplify constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem requires one value to be the average of two others, or when linear relationships between variables are implied.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis with Constraint Decomposition
general_skills.principle: Split problems into cases based on the presence or absence of specific elements (e.g., zero) that affect validity, then compute contributions from each case separately.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When constraints like leading zeros or distinctness require separating valid and invalid configurations.

general_skills.title: Permutation Adjustment for Validity
general_skills.principle: Calculate total permutations and subtract invalid ones (e.g., those violating digit constraints) to determine valid configurations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When counting arrangements where certain positions (e.g., leading digits) have restricted values.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Geometry Modeling
general_skills.principle: Assign coordinates to geometric figures to compute areas and proportions by leveraging algebraic relationships between points.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves spatial relationships or requires precise area calculations with known symmetry or divisions.

general_skills.title: Area Decomposition
general_skills.principle: Break complex regions into simpler, known shapes (e.g., triangles, trapezoids) to compute their areas through additive or subtractive methods.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When direct area computation of a region is infeasible, but its components can be analyzed individually.

general_skills.title: Symmetry-Driven Proportionality
general_skills.principle: Use symmetry and equal-width divisions to infer proportional relationships between regions, enabling fraction calculations without full area computations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When regions are defined by symmetric or evenly spaced divisions, and the goal is to compare their relative sizes.

general_skills.title: Recognize Structural Forms of Numbers
general_skills.principle: Identify numbers with specific divisor counts by analyzing their prime factorization structures (e.g., product of two distinct primes or prime cubes).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves constraints on the number of divisors or requires characterizing numbers based on their factorization.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis via Structural Decomposition
general_skills.principle: Split problems into distinct cases based on the possible forms of numbers (e.g., prime powers vs. products) to systematically explore all valid configurations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiple structural possibilities exist for a mathematical object, decompose the problem into cases to cover all scenarios.

general_skills.title: Factorization and Prime Verification
general_skills.principle: Factor candidate numbers and check primality conditions to validate whether they satisfy the problem's constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When verifying if a number meets specific criteria involving divisors, primes, or factor pairs.

general_skills.title: Structural Recognition
general_skills.principle: Identify mathematical structures (e.g., trees) implied by constraints like unique paths between nodes, leveraging graph theory principles to reduce the problem to a known combinatorial framework.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem involves connectivity constraints (e.g., unique paths, no cycles) and discrete entities (e.g., cities, nodes).

general_skills.title: Combinatorial Enumeration via Formulas
general_skills.principle: Apply established combinatorial formulas (e.g., Cayley's formula for labeled trees) to count configurations, combining them with other combinatorial factors (e.g., integer partitions) to compute total possibilities.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem requires counting distinct configurations with multiplicative components (e.g., structures × cost assignments).

general_skills.title: Modular Arithmetic Simplification
general_skills.principle: Use modular arithmetic (e.g., modulo 100) to compute final results efficiently, exploiting properties of divisibility and exponents to eliminate large intermediate values.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem requires the last few digits of a large number or involves constraints on total sums (e.g., budget utilization).

general_skills.title: Reciprocal Sum Coverage
general_skills.principle: When partitioning a set into subsets with specific frequencies, ensure the sum of reciprocals of their step sizes equals 1 to guarantee complete coverage.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem requires a partition of integers or elements into disjoint subsets with defined step sizes.

general_skills.title: GCD Overlap Prevention
general_skills.principle: Use gcd conditions between step sizes and starting positions to ensure arithmetic progressions do not overlap, maintaining distinct coverage.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When sequences are defined by arithmetic progressions and must avoid overlapping elements.

general_skills.title: Constraint-Driven Case Analysis
general_skills.principle: Generate candidate solutions by systematically exploring permutations of variables that satisfy primary constraints, then validate against secondary conditions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiple variables interact under restrictive constraints, and exhaustive enumeration is feasible.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis for Positional Constraints
general_skills.principle: When solving probability problems with ordered elements, split the problem into cases based on relative positions of key variables to compute favorable outcomes.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem involves dependencies between positions or ranges of values (e.g., card numbers, time intervals).

general_skills.title: Algebraic Simplification of Combinatorial Probabilities
general_skills.principle: Convert combinatorial expressions into algebraic forms to derive a probability function, enabling analytical simplification and comparison.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When calculating probabilities involving combinations or permutations with variable parameters.

general_skills.title: Quadratic Optimization for Thresholds
general_skills.principle: Solve quadratic inequalities to find thresholds where a function meets a condition, leveraging the function's parabolic behavior and domain constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a probability or value function is quadratic and requires finding minima/maxima within a bounded range.

general_skills.title: Polynomial Divisibility Constraints
general_skills.principle: Use the property that for polynomials with integer coefficients, $ P(x) - P(y) $ is divisible by $ x - y $ to derive necessary divisibility conditions on $ M $.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem involves polynomials with integer coefficients and requires constraints on their values at specific points.

general_skills.title: LCM of Divisors for Universality
general_skills.principle: Ensure $ M $ is a multiple of the least common multiple (LCM) of all required divisors to guarantee divisibility for arbitrary integers.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiple divisibility conditions must hold simultaneously for all possible integer inputs.

general_skills.title: Minimality Verification via Counterexamples
general_skills.principle: Test smaller candidate values of $ M $ to confirm they fail for some choice of integers, thereby proving the minimal valid $ M $.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When verifying that a candidate value is the smallest possible satisfying all constraints.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis Based on Primality
general_skills.principle: When analyzing divisibility conditions involving primes, split the problem into cases based on whether the divisor is prime or composite, and evaluate each case's validity through modular arithmetic or direct computation.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves a divisor expression that depends on prime parameters and requires checking divisibility constraints.

general_skills.title: Modular Arithmetic and Order Constraints
general_skills.principle: Use modular arithmetic to derive necessary conditions for divisibility, such as requiring the order of a base number modulo the divisor to divide the exponent, thereby constraining possible solutions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When verifying divisibility of expressions like $ a^k - 1 $ by a number, analyze the order of $ a $ modulo the divisor.

general_skills.title: Example-Based Elimination of Invalid Cases
general_skills.principle: Test small primes or specific instances to eliminate invalid cases, especially when general algebraic methods are insufficient to resolve ambiguities.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When verifying conjectures about prime parameters or complex divisibility conditions where theoretical analysis is inconclusive.

general_skills.title: Balance Products via Distribution
general_skills.principle: Distribute larger numbers across different groups to balance their products, preventing any single group from accumulating disproportionately large values.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When minimizing the maximum product of grouped elements with a fixed set of numbers.

general_skills.title: Total Product Constraint Analysis
general_skills.principle: Use the total product of all elements to establish a lower bound for the maximum group product by comparing it to the cube of a candidate value.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When verifying the minimality of a maximum product in partitioning problems.

general_skills.title: Constructive Grouping with Pairing
general_skills.principle: Pair large numbers with small numbers in groups to balance their contributions to the product, ensuring even distribution of magnitude across groups.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When creating explicit groupings to achieve balanced products in combinatorial optimization.

general_skills.title: Algebraic Substitution for Variable Reduction
general_skills.principle: Express relationships between variables to reduce the problem to a single variable, simplifying constraints and target quantities.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiple variables are involved and a direct relationship exists between them.

general_skills.title: Square Root Constraints to Perfect Squares
general_skills.principle: Transform equations involving square roots into conditions requiring perfect squares, leveraging algebraic identities to derive constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When sums or differences of square roots are tied to integer outputs with specific properties (e.g., non-perfect squares).

general_skills.title: Systematic Candidate Testing with Constraints
general_skills.principle: Iterate through plausible candidate values while verifying constraints, prioritizing extremes to maximize/minimize target quantities.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analytical solutions are complex but discrete candidates exist within bounded ranges.

general_skills.title: Derive Variable Relationships from Inequalities
general_skills.principle: Combine multiple inequalities to establish direct relationships between variables, narrowing down possible assignments by eliminating contradictions or overlaps.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiple inequalities involve the same or related variables, use logical deduction to infer constraints on their possible values.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis Based on Constrained Variables
general_skills.principle: Split the problem into cases by prioritizing variables with the fewest possible values, then systematically test each case against all constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When variables have limited possible values due to constraints, use case analysis to explore valid assignments while maintaining consistency.

general_skills.title: Constraint-Driven Elimination
general_skills.principle: For each case, iteratively eliminate invalid subcases by verifying all constraints, ensuring no contradictions arise in the assignment of values.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When testing potential assignments, validate each step against all given constraints to discard invalid possibilities early.

general_skills.title: Substitute Polynomial Identities
general_skills.principle: When a variable satisfies a known polynomial equation, substitute that equation to replace terms and simplify expressions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When working with roots of equations that have known minimal polynomials (e.g., roots of unity).

general_skills.title: Expand and Simplify Products
general_skills.principle: Expand algebraic products and apply identities to reduce complexity, leveraging known relationships between terms.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When evaluating products involving variables with defined algebraic properties (e.g., roots of unity).

general_skills.title: Balance Ratio Components
general_skills.principle: Minimize a ratio by optimizing the denominator while keeping the numerator as small as possible, recognizing trade-offs between increasing the denominator and the numerator's growth.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When optimizing a ratio where the numerator and denominator are competing factors.

general_skills.title: Maximize Denominator for Minimal Numerator
general_skills.principle: For a given structure (e.g., digit positions), maximize the denominator (e.g., digit sum) by setting non-critical components to their maximum values while minimizing the numerator.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the goal is to maximize a denominator (e.g., digit sum) while keeping the numerator (e.g., number value) minimal.

general_skills.title: Systematic Candidate Testing
general_skills.principle: Test candidates with high denominator values systematically, comparing their ratios to identify the optimal solution.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When evaluating discrete candidates for a minimal/maximal ratio, prioritize those with high denominator values.

general_skills.title: Two-Step Constraint Validation
general_skills.principle: Identify candidates by checking for a primary condition (e.g., column maximum) and then validate against a secondary condition (e.g., row minimum).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving problems requiring an element to satisfy multiple constraints (e.g., being both a maximum in one dimension and a minimum in another).

general_skills.title: Systematic Iteration
general_skills.principle: Methodically evaluate each element in a structured data set by iterating through rows/columns and applying targeted checks.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing matrices or grids to find elements meeting specific relational criteria (e.g., maxima/minima across dimensions).

general_skills.title: Divisor Function Translation
general_skills.principle: Convert divisor count requirements into exponent relationships using the formula $ (e_1 + 1)(e_2 + 1)... $ for prime factorizations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem specifies the number of divisors for a number or its powers.

general_skills.title: Factorization Case Analysis
general_skills.principle: Decompose the target divisor count into integer products to generate candidate exponent configurations for prime factorizations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving problems involving multiplicative constraints on divisors or exponents.

general_skills.title: Constraint-Driven Optimization
general_skills.principle: Systematically evaluate and compare candidate solutions to identify the minimal value satisfying all constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When optimizing for minimal/maximal values under specific mathematical conditions.

general_skills.title: Total Outcomes via Combinations
general_skills.principle: Calculate the total number of possible outcomes using combinations when selecting items from a finite set. This forms the denominator in probability calculations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining the total number of possible selections in a probability problem involving random sampling without replacement.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis for Target Value
general_skills.principle: Split the problem into distinct cases based on possible combinations of elements that could satisfy the target value or condition. Evaluate each case's validity against the problem constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem requires identifying valid configurations of elements that meet a specific numerical or structural target.

general_skills.title: Constraint-Driven Elimination
general_skills.principle: Systematically eliminate invalid cases by verifying each case against the problem's constraints, ensuring only valid combinations contribute to the solution.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When narrowing down valid outcomes from a set of possible cases by checking against explicit constraints or target conditions.

general_skills.title: Area Division for Dimension Constraints
general_skills.principle: Divide the total area by the number of required pieces to determine the area of each piece, then identify integer dimensions that satisfy this area and fit within the original shape's constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dividing a shape into congruent pieces with no leftover space, use area division to constrain possible dimensions.

general_skills.title: Configuration Exploration Within Bounds
general_skills.principle: Systematically enumerate all valid arrangements of smaller shapes within the original dimensions, ensuring congruence, fit, and no gaps or overlaps.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving problems requiring partitioning a shape into congruent parts, explore all possible configurations that respect spatial constraints.

general_skills.title: Perimeter Extremum Identification
general_skills.principle: Calculate perimeters for all valid configurations and compare them to determine the maximum and minimum values, then compute their difference.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When optimizing perimeters or other measures across multiple configurations, compute and compare values for each valid case.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis
general_skills.principle: Split the problem into distinct cases based on the number of elements satisfying a constraint to ensure all valid combinations are counted.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When constraints require considering multiple scenarios (e.g., minimum/maximum counts of specific elements).

general_skills.title: Complementary Counting
general_skills.principle: Subtract the number of invalid combinations from the total to find the valid count when direct counting is complex.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When invalid cases are easier to count than valid ones, especially with exclusionary constraints.

general_skills.title: Fixing Required Elements
general_skills.principle: Recognize and fix required elements (e.g., mandatory selections) to reduce the problem's complexity and simplify counting.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem enforces mandatory components that must be included in all valid solutions.

general_skills.title: Factor Polynomials for Root Analysis
general_skills.principle: Break down complex polynomials into simpler components (e.g., quadratics) to apply root conditions individually, such as discriminant requirements for real roots.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing polynomials with variable coefficients and needing to ensure all roots are real.

general_skills.title: Solve Parameter Inequalities via Critical Points
general_skills.principle: Identify critical points where conditions change (e.g., discriminant zero) and analyze intervals between them to determine valid parameter ranges.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining ranges of parameters that satisfy specific mathematical constraints.

general_skills.title: Compute Probabilities via Interval Measures
general_skills.principle: Calculate the probability by measuring the length of favorable intervals relative to the total interval length, then simplify the resulting fraction.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with uniform probability distributions over continuous intervals.

general_skills.title: Use Trigonometric Identities to Simplify Inverse Function Sums
general_skills.principle: When dealing with sums of inverse trigonometric functions, apply identities like arctan(u) + arctan(v) = π/2 if uv = 1 to reduce complexity and derive algebraic relationships.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When an equation involves sums of inverse trigonometric functions that must hold for all values of a variable.

general_skills.title: Transform Equations Using Tangent to Eliminate Inverse Functions
general_skills.principle: Take the tangent of both sides of an equation involving inverse trigonometric functions to convert it into an algebraic equation, leveraging the identity tan(arctan(x)) = x.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When functional equations with inverse trigonometric terms need to be simplified into algebraic forms for further analysis.

general_skills.title: Solve Systems of Equations Derived from Functional Constraints
general_skills.principle: Once relationships between variables are established through identities or transformations, solve the resulting system of equations to determine unknown constants.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiple equations involving variables must be solved simultaneously to find their values.

general_skills.title: Parity-Based Case Analysis
general_skills.principle: Categorize combinations by parity (even/odd) to determine valid sum conditions. For even sums, consider cases like all even numbers or two odds and one even.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem requires sums with specific parity constraints.

general_skills.title: Exclusion via Subtraction
general_skills.principle: Calculate total valid cases and subtract those that violate additional constraints (e.g., sum thresholds) to refine the count.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When there are exclusion criteria that require removing invalid subsets from the total.

general_skills.title: Structured Case Splitting
general_skills.principle: Split the problem into distinct, non-overlapping cases based on constraints, compute each case separately, and combine results.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiple scenarios contribute to the solution and require independent analysis.

general_skills.title: Apply Summation Identities
general_skills.principle: Recognize and apply standard summation formulas (e.g., sum of cubes) to simplify complex expressions into manageable algebraic forms.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When encountering sums of powers or sequences that can be expressed with known closed-form formulas.

general_skills.title: Transform Equations via Substitution
general_skills.principle: Simplify equations by substituting known identities or variable substitutions, reducing them to solvable forms (e.g., Pell's equation).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When faced with complex equations that can be decomposed or rewritten using algebraic manipulation and standard identities.

general_skills.title: Solve Diophantine Equations with Recursive Relations
general_skills.principle: Leverage recursive relations or known solution patterns (e.g., Pell's equation) to find integer solutions under modular or inequality constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving for integer variables in equations involving modular conditions or quadratic forms.

general_skills.title: Trigonometric Ratio Application
general_skills.principle: Use trigonometric identities in right triangles to relate angles and side lengths, enabling derivation of unknown quantities through ratio-based equations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When given angles and side lengths in right triangles, or when angles' trigonometric values are provided.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Geometry Modeling
general_skills.principle: Assign coordinates to geometric points to translate spatial relationships into algebraic equations, facilitating computation of distances and intersections.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When geometric configurations involve multiple points with relative positions that can be expressed numerically.

general_skills.title: Pythagorean Theorem Utilization
general_skills.principle: Apply the Pythagorean theorem to compute distances in right triangles by solving equations derived from squared side relationships.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When calculating distances between points in right triangles or verifying orthogonality in geometric figures.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis
general_skills.principle: Split complex constraints into distinct cases based on the structure of the problem, ensuring each case addresses unique aspects of the constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem involves multiple overlapping conditions that require different handling strategies.

general_skills.title: Combinatorial Counting
general_skills.principle: Use combinations and permutations to calculate the number of valid arrangements after defining the structure of the problem and eliminating invalid cases.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem requires counting configurations with specific repetition or arrangement rules.

general_skills.title: Constraint Enforcement
general_skills.principle: Systematically eliminate invalid cases by ensuring all problem constraints are explicitly satisfied in each scenario.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the problem requires strict adherence to constraints that limit valid configurations.

general_skills.title: Coordinate Geometry Modeling
general_skills.principle: Translate geometric configurations into coordinate systems to enable algebraic computation of distances, slopes, and intersections.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When a problem involves geometric figures with unknown coordinates or requires precise distance/angle calculations.

general_skills.title: Pythagorean Theorem Application
general_skills.principle: Use the Pythagorean theorem to determine missing side lengths in right triangles, leveraging known side lengths and relationships.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving for unknown lengths in right-angled triangles or verifying geometric constraints.

general_skills.title: Parallelism Proportionality
general_skills.principle: Establish proportional relationships between segments using parallelism conditions (e.g., slopes or vector equivalences) to derive coordinate relationships.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When parallel lines or vectors are involved, to relate segment lengths or positions algebraically.

general_skills.title: Model Constraints as Forbidden Positions
general_skills.principle: Reframe the problem as counting permutations with restricted positions (e.g., forbidden columns for specific rows) to leverage combinatorial structures like rook polynomials or permutation restrictions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When constraints involve avoiding specific assignments in a combinatorial arrangement (e.g., permutations, placements).

general_skills.title: Case Analysis for Overlapping Constraints
general_skills.principle: Split the problem into cases based on whether forbidden elements (e.g., corner squares) are included, then compute valid configurations for each case while accounting for overlaps.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiple constraints interact (e.g., overlapping forbidden positions) and direct computation is infeasible.

general_skills.title: Inclusion-Exclusion for Adjusting Overcounts
general_skills.principle: Subtract invalid cases introduced by constraints, then add back over-subtracted overlaps using inclusion-exclusion principles to ensure accurate final counts.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When calculating totals requires eliminating invalid configurations while avoiding double-counting corrections.

general_skills.title: Factorable Equation Transformation
general_skills.principle: Rearrange the equation to a form amenable to factoring by adding/subtracting constants, enabling the application of techniques like Simon's Favorite Factoring Trick (SFFT).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with Diophantine equations involving products and linear terms.

general_skills.title: Factor Pair Enumeration
general_skills.principle: Generate all integer factor pairs of a constant term derived from the transformed equation to identify potential solutions.
general_skills.when_to_apply: After transforming an equation into a product form, when seeking integer solutions.

general_skills.title: Solution Verification
general_skills.principle: Substitute candidate solutions back into the original equation to confirm validity and eliminate extraneous results.
general_skills.when_to_apply: After generating potential solutions to ensure they satisfy the original problem constraints.

general_skills.title: Generate Sets via Quadratic Expressions
general_skills.principle: Systematically evaluate all elements of a finite field to construct sets defined by quadratic forms (e.g., squares or squares plus constants).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing intersections or unions of sets defined by quadratic expressions in finite fields.

general_skills.title: Compute Intersections via Element Comparison
general_skills.principle: Determine the intersection of two sets by directly comparing their elements, leveraging explicit enumeration or structural properties.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the cardinality of sets is small or their elements can be explicitly listed.

general_skills.title: Leverage Finite Field Properties
general_skills.principle: Use known properties of finite fields (e.g., quadratic residue counts) to infer set structures or validate results.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When working with modular arithmetic and needing to predict or verify set sizes without exhaustive computation.

general_skills.title: Binomial Probability Recognition
general_skills.principle: Identify scenarios with independent trials, two possible outcomes, and a fixed success probability, which can be modeled using the binomial distribution formula.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When calculating probabilities for exactly k successes in n independent trials with a constant success probability.

general_skills.title: Combination-Based Probability Calculation
general_skills.principle: Compute probabilities for specific outcome counts by multiplying combinations (n choose k) with the appropriate powers of success and failure probabilities.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When determining the likelihood of a precise number of successes in a fixed number of independent trials.

general_skills.title: Fraction Simplification via GCD
general_skills.principle: Reduce fractions to their lowest terms by dividing numerator and denominator by their greatest common divisor, ensuring the final answer meets required formatting constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When expressing probabilities as reduced fractions and summing numerator and denominator for final output.

general_skills.title: Structural Deduction from Divisibility
general_skills.principle: If a number divides an exponential expression, infer constraints on its prime factors or structure (e.g., n must be a power of 3 if it divides 3^n).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing divisibility conditions involving exponents and prime factors.

general_skills.title: Modular Arithmetic Simplification
general_skills.principle: Use modular arithmetic properties (e.g., Euler’s theorem) to reduce complex divisibility checks to manageable computations.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When verifying divisibility of expressions like a^k mod m or solving congruences.

general_skills.title: Case Analysis via Small Values
general_skills.principle: Systematically test small integers to identify initial solutions or patterns, then generalize or refine constraints.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When searching for minimal solutions in number-theoretic problems with discrete constraints.

general_skills.title: Place Value Decomposition
general_skills.principle: Break numbers into their digit-based components (e.g., thousands, hundreds) to form algebraic equations representing their structure.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When dealing with digit-based problems involving unknown digits or positional constraints.

general_skills.title: Equation Simplification via Like-Term Combination
general_skills.principle: Combine like terms in equations to reduce complexity and isolate variables for systematic solving.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When handling algebraic expressions with repeated patterns or overlapping terms.

general_skills.title: Constraint-Driven Iterative Solving
general_skills.principle: Use domain-specific constraints (e.g., digit limits) to narrow solution possibilities and iteratively test valid values.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving for discrete variables with bounded ranges, such as digits in number theory problems.

general_skills.title: Logarithmic Change of Base
general_skills.principle: Convert logarithms between bases using the change of base formula to simplify expressions or enable cancellation.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When solving equations with variables in exponents or simplifying products of logarithms with different bases.

general_skills.title: Telescoping Logarithmic Products
general_skills.principle: Recognize patterns where consecutive logarithmic terms in a product cancel out, leaving a simplified result.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When multiplying multiple logarithms with bases forming a cyclic chain (e.g., log_b(a) * log_a(c) * log_c(b)).
